subject: They will never stop coming for our right to vote

body:
Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote. They simply don't believe we all deserve to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052426_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
KATU: Vance calls on Congressional Republicans to pass SAVE Act during speech [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052426_2&amount=25]
Opponents of voting rights are trying everything they can think of to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address Trump's often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. Vice President J.D. Vance called on Congress again this week, begging them to pass this awful bill ahead of the next election.
The SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now, Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052426_2&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052426_2&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=052426_2&amount=35]
How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052426_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

body:
Newsletter

---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| ENERGY FORWARD
---
| Hi friends, These past few weeks were another reminder of what makes Wyoming special. Everywhere Kelly and I traveled, we met people investing in their communities, building businesses, mentoring young people, supporting local jobs, and thinking seriously about the future of our state. One thing I’ve always appreciated about Wyoming Republicans is that we still understand politics starts with neighbors talking to neighbors. Real conversations about how we keep Wyoming the best place to live, work, raise a family, and build a future. Spending time around the state has shown me that this idea is still important to our citizens. That spirit is on display. From Lincoln Day gatherings and community events to conversations about energy, entrepreneurship, and workforce development, there’s a shared understanding that Wyoming succeeds when people stay involved, work together, and keep showing up for their communities. We have had more support come our way from the energy industry. Nathan McLeland from M&K Oil is someone I have known and worked with regularly, and we have accomplished a lot for energy together. I have always believed Wyoming has an opportunity to lead, not follow, when it comes to powering America’s future. Our energy workers, producers, engineers, and communities have helped build this country for generations, and Wyoming should never be afraid to stand behind the industries and people who keep the lights on. From innovative companies to energy leaders to volunteers and community organizations helping young people across the state, a lot is happening in Wyoming energy worth believing in. I am also continuing to show up and do the Senate work I was elected to do. This meant attending the Transportation Committee in Casper. There are still critical interim conversations to be had. Thank you to everyone who welcomed us over the past few weeks, shared ideas, hosted events, and continues to support this campaign. We’re grateful for the chance to keep earning your trust one town at a time. \- Eric
---
| | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KSE761QB2BESTKV6K14SSVMA_1)
---
| **In Case You Missed It** I formally filed to be your next Republican Governor last Saturday. I had some great backup from the Cody Youth for Justice group and Kelly.

As election day nears, the campaign will be working hard to reach each voter across the state, and to do that, we could use your support!

Consider chipping in today!
---

[Politics in park prove positive](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KSE761QB2BESTKV6K14SSVMA_4) Your Wyoming Link [Gubernatorial candidate Eric Barlow focuses on Wyoming’s future](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KSE761QB2BESTKV6K14SSVMA_5) Oil City News [Natrona County students share concerns with gubernatorial candidate at Thursday event](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KSE761QB2BESTKV6K14SSVMA_6)
---
|
---
| |
---
| -American Legion Memorial Day Service, Monday, May 25 · 10-11AM, Jackson Town Square, 10 E Broadway, Jackson, WY -Hootenany at the Pink Garter Theater, Monday, May 25 · 5:30 - 9PM
50 W Broadway, Jackson, WY -Coffee with the Barlows, Wednesday, May 27 · 6–9 AM Fossil Fuel Coffee Company, 819 S Main St, Kemmerer, WY
Economic Opportunities & Challenges -May 27, 12-1:30PM, Holiday Inn, 1675 Sunset Dr., Rock Springs
-Lunch at Marbleton Senior Center, Thursday, May 28 · 11:30 - 1PM 429 2nd St, Big Piney, WY

-"Community Concert for Hope" Orr's Hope Foundation, Thursday, May 28, 5-8PM, N David Street, Casper, WY
---
| **On The Trail**
---
|
---
| | | GILLETTE
As a former educator who continues to work with youth at all levels, Kelly wasn't missing a chance to read to students from the local elementary schools in Campbell County through the Wyoming Reads Program. Each student gets to go home with the book they have chosen. Such a great experience!
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | LARAMIE
I attended the Wyoming Energy Authority's Next Frontier Energy Summit in Laramie. It's a key event that offers Wyoming's energy stakeholders a place to learn, collaborate, and network as they build the future of Wyoming's economy.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | CASPER
We got a tour of the Wyo Sports Ranch. It was good to see firsthand what the project is bringing to Casper and the surrounding community. Developments like this help create opportunity, support local businesses, and keep communities moving forward. Then we stopped by DISA Technologies with Greyson Buckingham and John Lee. They launched the company after getting their start through the UW Ellbogen $50K Entrepreneurship Competition, and they're doing some really innovative work in mineral recovery and mine remediation. It's always good to see Wyoming people building businesses, creating jobs, and deciding to do it here at home instead of somewhere else. I appreciate getting tours and the chance to meet the teams behind the work.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **CASPER**
---
| | | Kelly and I had a great time in Casper. Jan and Brad Cundy hosted us at the Boys & Girls Club of Glenrock, where we had the chance to hear from Anthony Robles. Anthony shared his story and the message behind his book and the new Netflix film Unstoppable. It was great to see the impact an event like this can have on young people and the community.
Then we stopped by High Country Fabrication in Casper. I always appreciate the opportunity to meet the people behind Wyoming businesses and see the work being done firsthand. Businesses like this help support local jobs, strengthen communities, and keep Wyoming moving forward.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | WORLAND It was great to join Republicans in Washakie County for their Lincoln Day Dinner. These gatherings are a good reminder that our party is strongest when neighbors come together, share ideas, and stay involved in the work of keeping Wyoming the best place to live, work, and raise a family.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | CHEYENNE Kelly and I had a great morning in Cheyenne at the Boys & Girls Club Breakfast. We were both inspired by Orion Jean and his message about kindness, leadership, and service. His Race to Kindness is a good reminder that you do not have to wait until you are grown up to make a real difference in your community. Boys & Girls Clubs do important work for kids and families across Wyoming, providing encouragement, opportunity, and a place where young people can grow and thrive
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | CASPER Kelly and I had a great time at the Wyoming Trucking Association event in Casper. It was informative to hear about what's happening in the industry across Wyoming and beyond. We also had the chance to talk (and be bear hugged) by Wyoming Olympian Rulon Gardner about kids participating in sports and the impact those opportunities can have on young people.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **BIGHORN BASIN**
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| Kelly and I had a great couple of days across the Big Horn Basin, with stops in Lovell, Greybull, Cowley, Frannie, and Deaver. We started with coffee at the Mustang Cafe, toured Queen Bee Gardens with the Zeller family, visited New Horizons Care Center and Lovell’s hospital and clinic, and stopped by S & L Industrial to learn more about their work keeping road construction projects safe across Wyoming. We also toured Dauntless Fitness with Stacy and Devin Bair of Bairco Construction, another good example of Wyoming people investing in their communities and building places where families can live, work, and stay. I appreciated visiting with the mayors of Cowley, Frannie, Deaver, and Lovell about the opportunities and challenges facing their towns. We wrapped up with a great meet and greet at The Bull Pub and a fundraiser at the Cowley Community Center. Thank you to everyone who took time to visit with us and share what matters most across the Basin.
---
|
---

body:

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe42a49a-51e8-488a-bc6e-afacd9ae0ed6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The South Korean stock market is booming. The KOSPI index is [up about 150% from its April 2025 low](https://substack.com/redirect/7b649c1f-7396-4c70-abc8-4907c8cbd1d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and gained ~75% percent in 2025. This is Korea's best performance in over 25 years. But it hasn't stopped this year. It's already up more than 75% and recently touched the 8,000 level for the first time in history. For comparison, it was hovering around 2,500 two years ago.
Regular readers know I've had a lifelong interest in bubbles. Unsurprisingly, performance like this catches my attention. Six days after hitting 8,000, the KOSPI plunged around 12%, triggering downside circuit breakers. The very next day it [bounced 8%](https://substack.com/redirect/d01c6ac3-4fcb-471e-8b85-1c462a418725?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or so, triggering _an upside_ circuit breaker. It was starting to look less like a rally and more like a seizure. My bubble spotting seismograph was indicating tremors afoot.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/73732be4-96c8-4c60-bb39-51b3c53c11b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/KOSPI:IND](https://substack.com/redirect/e9deca8f-8b3d-4004-8042-6e1205d1f333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The dynamics get more concerning when you acknowledge that the meteoric rally has been largely fueled by the performance of two stocks: **Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix**. Both make the high-bandwidth memory chips that power Nvidia's AI accelerators, and as the media put it bluntly: ["Without Samsung and Hynix, there would be no KOSPI at 6,000"](https://substack.com/redirect/3e682bf8-e188-419a-8560-47730e2e7387?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (not to mention 8,000).
## [The Power of Foxy Thinking](https://substack.com/redirect/30eeadb5-d33b-4177-b852-e4276d51456e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| February 16, 2012
[](https://substack.com/redirect/30eeadb5-d33b-4177-b852-e4276d51456e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/30eeadb5-d33b-4177-b852-e4276d51456e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/30eeadb5-d33b-4177-b852-e4276d51456e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So, the question I ask myself is simple: Is this a bubble?
[My 2011 book on bubbles](https://substack.com/redirect/cc3fbdf2-85fc-4aa2-9dd9-3404270bc9bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) provided a framework for thinking about how to answer this question. The book was based upon a class I taught at Yale, and offered a multi-lens approach to spotting bubbles before they burst. I suggested the use of five lenses (microeconomics, macroeconomics, psychology, politics, and biology) to explore and evaluate sustainability of a boom. At root, it was based on my belief that every perspective is limited, biased, and incomplete...so why not use more than one?
So, let's run the KOSPI through my framework.
**Microeconomics Lens = Bubbly**
Traditional economics suggests that when prices rise, demand is depressed and supply is motivated. But what if the opposite happens? What if higher prices lead to more demand? Might a self-fulfilling dynamic of higher prices leading to higher demand lead to even higher prices (and even higher demand)?
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..qidC_55SRtDiXxpjeWEqbRq5RV8ZmYGyxgKLjvN0xZY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199106701)
The KOSPI is a capitalization weighted index, meaning that the large companies exert more influence on the index. It also means that as heavyweights like Samsung rise in value faster than other components, their weight in the index rises. Continued positive performance compounds this dynamic, leading to a narrowing of breadth and a limited set of companies that drive the index performance. Today, Hynix and Samsung are about 50% of the index...and their earnings depend on a bet that AI infrastructure keeps booming. KB Securities [calls this "a textbook feature of a late-stage bubble"](https://substack.com/redirect/e02f0e95-92d8-42e3-83b1-cb32d4f2344e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): narrowing leadership, concentration in a few names, retail money piling in behind them. It's what happened with the [Nifty Fifty](https://substack.com/redirect/f0271e1e-63b6-45f0-8453-e8c8f564d2dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 1971 and the dotcom stocks in 1999.

**Macroeconomics Lens = Bubbly**
When investors can easily borrow money to invest, my alarm bells go off because this too can create a bubbly dynamic. And through this lens, Korea looks vulnerable. [Margin loan balances hit a record $27 billion on May 15](https://substack.com/redirect/d01c6ac3-4fcb-471e-8b85-1c462a418725?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the very same day the KOSPI touched 8,000. And because the margin interest rates are hovering in the 7%-9% range, this implies retail investors are convinced the index will do better.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e2dfc1e5-90de-4ac7-9a37-d3c94bd6fe85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seoul_Skyline_including_Lotte_Tower_3.png](https://substack.com/redirect/e5f73d02-3ab4-413a-ae96-9b67b51954bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Credit magnifies both the upside and the downside. Think of it as a two-edged sword, and slight changes in credit can turn a virtuous upside cycle into a vicious downside one. Consider the story of a [Korean civil servant](https://substack.com/redirect/71cf4284-304e-4465-898f-6b6ca53834d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who put 2.3 billion won ($1.7 million) into Hynix, most of it borrowed. Might that end badly? When the KOSPI dropped 12 percent, [forced liquidations surged to 6.5 percent of unsettled trades](https://substack.com/redirect/0fc8cbee-44e1-4fa0-9265-f016d39470d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [$625 billion in market value vanished in a single session](https://substack.com/redirect/70b0f507-007c-4c93-b417-8285abfac12c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**Psychology Lens = Bubbly**
Anyone who studies financial bubbles understands that investors swing between greed and fear. Times with widespread and extreme investor fear are usually good times to buy. The flip side is that widespread and extreme investor greed is a good time to sell. And while data such as foreign investor selling may dampen bubble concerns, Korean retail investors are suffering from stratospheric levels of FOMO (fear of missing out). They've absorbed more than $13.2 billion of foreign investor selling last week alone and are doing so with margin debt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e14d33d-63d8-41b3-b438-d40661f6f164?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Investor overconfidence is a tell-tale sign of bubbly conditions and record Korean margin debt and buying in the face of intense selling from foreigners seems to be pointing to a bubbly KOSPI. ZeroHedge recently called Korean retail investors ["levered to the gills and out of funds, buying with the bank's money."](https://substack.com/redirect/45010ff9-37ba-4c3f-b186-99fb4b68c779?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) South Koreans are even [cashing out insurance policies](https://substack.com/redirect/532c1768-8b87-4ec5-8fb8-faf552e91de2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to play the market, eerily reminiscent of the ordinary people flooding the market for tulip bulbs in 1637, with some even mortgaging their homes. When the smart money exits and the crowd doubles down on borrowed cash, it's starting to look as bubbly as a glass of champagne.
**Political Lens = Sort of Bubbly.**
Government actions often also play role in fueling bubbles. This was true in the great financial crisis as government policies created moral hazard in the mortgage market, allowing a social objective of greater homeownership to create and reinforce risky lending. Political leaders thinking about market performance as a report card for their political acumen is also a concerning dynamic.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..qidC_55SRtDiXxpjeWEqbRq5RV8ZmYGyxgKLjvN0xZY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199106701)
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung [vowed to hit KOSPI 5,000](https://substack.com/redirect/b672f7b4-5766-49b6-8601-aefed12f518e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and his "Corporate Value-up Program 2.0" mandated governance reforms, strengthened shareholder protections, and [slashed dividend income tax in half to 25%](https://substack.com/redirect/866d26b0-e196-4883-94af-7b243b3d7cb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). These are real, structural improvements. But when a government explicitly targets a stock index number, it creates a political incentive to keep the party going--and a political cost to letting it correct.
**Biology Lens = Bubbly.**
In the past, I've often described a bubble as an infection that spreads rapidly across a society, eventually reaching epidemic breadth before "herd immunity" leads to a correction. The AI narrative is a great case in point, and it's jumped from Silicon Valley to Seoul in less than two years. Samsung's HBM4 chips, SK Hynix's Nvidia contracts, and the "semiconductor supercycle" are all mechanisms to spread the AI virus to more and more people. _The Korea Times_ identified it as a ["gray rhino": plainly visible, widely recognized, and frequently underestimated](https://substack.com/redirect/b672f7b4-5766-49b6-8601-aefed12f518e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The number of people without any exposure to the artificial intelligence story is dwindling rapidly.
* * *
## [AI Infrastructure: Boom or Bust?](https://substack.com/redirect/66135570-c49e-4406-8629-27c3bccd12e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[In the late 1990s, Lucent Technologies was America's most widely held stock -- a "picks and shovels" play on the internet revolution. The company lent billions to its own customers so they could buy more Lucent equipment. On paper, revenue soared. In reality, Lucent was financing its own demand. When the customers went bust, Lucent nearly followed. The p...](https://substack.com/redirect/66135570-c49e-4406-8629-27c3bccd12e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
Epidemics don't end because the virus weakens. They end when everyone susceptible has already been infected. And with the case of Artificial Intelligence, herd immunity is nigh. In markets, that means the rally ends when everyone who's going to buy has already bought--on margin, at the top. There are no more greater fools left to join the party. When taxicab drivers and bellman start talking about the market, the bubble is close to bursting.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/013ac3de-164b-4cb9-8053-402203a3a418?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**So where does this leave us?**
My assessment is that the Korean markets are very bubbly and unsustainable. Record margin debt, forced liquidations, and professional investors selling while retail investors sell life insurance to buy the market are big bright flashing warning signs. And the fact that everyone, and I mean everyone everywhere, is talking about AI adds a level of caution to anything dependent upon that story continuing.
I've often said that investors are destined to make mistakes. None of us is perfect. But **we do have a choice in the type of mistake to make**. There are errors of commission in which investors own a bubble that eventually leads to losses. And there are errors of omission in which investors miss the final stages of a bubble and miss gains.

Korea is not a market I'd chase. Yes the AI semiconductor story is real and Samsung and Hynix are world-class companies that will benefit from the global transformation underway. But a good story and a good investment are not the same thing, especially when leverage is maxed out, the institutions are heading for the exits, and the government is promising the party won't end. Now's the time to make errors of omission...

Peter,

In 2017, I left my practice as a pediatrician to run for Congress and advocate for the hard-working families of Washington's 8th District.

While so much has changed, **your support has remained constant**. And for that, I'll always be eternally grateful.

Thanks to your support, we've been able to accomplish a lot for working families. But there's still so much to do, which starts with unwinding the actions this administration has taken that are making life so much harder for people I represent. With this election set to determine the future of our country, there's too much at stake to leave things to chance.

clean_body: Peter, In 2017, I left my practice as a pediatrician to run for Congress and advocate for the hard-working families of Washington's 8th District. While so much has changed, your support has remained constant. And for that, I'll always be eternally grateful. Thanks to your support, we've been able to accomplish a lot for working families. But there's still so much to do, which starts with unwinding the actions this administration has taken that are making life so much harder for people I represent. With this election set to determine the future of our country, there's too much at stake to leave things to chance. Protecting abortion rights, securing access to affordable healthcare, putting patients and doctors back in the driver’s seat, cutting costs, putting working families first, making childcare affordable, protecting immigrant communities, and creating an economy that works for everyone — the future of these issues will pivot on the midterms and set the stage for 2028. # [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41406%2E3422442%2Es-pYWB)
Peter,
Here’s the reality in the California governor’s race:
With less than two weeks until the primary election, there’s a chance that **TWO** MAGA Republicans could end up on the general election ballot.
**We need a Democrat who stands out from the pack.** I’m not like most people running for governor. I'm a single mom of three kids who fills the gas tank and pushes the grocery cart just like almost everybody else in our state—and most of all, I can take accountability and laugh at myself too.
**That’s why we made this ad to cut through the noise and make sure voters across California hear what’s at stake.[You can check it out here:](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260524_3_ak.Vfy-ny&refcode=em20260524-41406&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41406%2E3422442%2Es-pYWB)**

With less than two weeks left until the primary, every day counts. I’m counting on supporters like you, Peter, to help us keep our message in front of voters when it matters most.

Katie

body:
Summer is about to get hectic

|
Hey, Friend, it's Steve Scalise.
I've got to warn you about something today.
The summer sprint is about to begin. You may be asking yourself: "What does that even mean?"
It means you're going to start getting messages left and right from people asking you to donate and making outlandish promises about what your donation will do.
It's enough to make your head spin.
So today I'm here to make a deal with you: [If you read my message today, you could probably ignore the others you'll get for the rest of the day](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z5f1epkbo1ub4jpcq162onkhha2kgvjidvln4vjg_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sti62o32c9h2bs).
Deal?
---
| | [YES](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zp30nqdejv68s1jqug1d4om0jg0e1ik3njmkv6p8_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sti62o32c9h2bs)
---
| | [NO](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zqk2hr4gj39jn8avvdp15efmprcp11hic6m2ccm0_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sti62o32c9h2bs)
---
Perfect!
Right now, our prospects for keeping our MAGA Majority this November are getting slimmer by the day, and it has me worried.
The DCCC is targeting 35 GOP seats across the country, and as it stands, we're stretched too thin to fight back in all 35 races.
I've watched as our fundraising has fallen off a cliff over the past two months.
If we don't change course immediately, President Trump's impeachment is exactly what we should expect if Democrats win the House Majority.
Don't just take it from us - President Trump himself is warning every Conservative: "If we don't win the midterms... they'll find a reason to impeach me."
It's completely possible to stop it, but it requires Patriots like you to step up immediately.
[I've set a goal to reach out to 10,000 MAGA Patriots to humbly ask each of you to chip in just $10 to save our House Majority and save President Trump from impeachment.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbsbg4c7hupkhnlt2dd74840nbpnnru68eaot8ko_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sti62o32c9h2bs)
I wouldn't be asking if the stakes weren't dire. Are you ready to step up to bat to when we need you most?

**Thank you. Not a single donation goes unnoticed, and I mean that. We 're in this fight together.**

name: Marsha Blackburn
subject: Honoring our brave men and women
body:
We must never forget the profound price they paid so that we may live in freedom in the greatest country in the world.

| | | | | | Peter,
Today is a solemn reminder of the brave men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our great nation.
Their courage, valor, and selflessness represent the very best of the American spirit.
We must never forget the profound price they paid so that we may live in freedom in the greatest country in the world.
Today, and every day, we owe an unpayable debt of gratitude to our fallen heroes and the families they left behind.
May God bless you, and may God bless the United States of America.
Sincerely,
Marsha Blackburn

## Iran Peace Deal Takes Shape
The U.S.-Iran agreement Trump says is "largely negotiated" includes a [60-day ceasefire extension](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u3CAQBeCnwR0WHv-AC4qNInc3TaSktLgwtifCYAG7zubpI_IKaedIo_Odnx_rhyFPYf9mTtRli2vAO3ssBdNKyYQLjUWHxp94xkTGO_O2KwiYuBg5jKsz5N_r0Di9IQL2DepOylmKXqmhOXT3CeMnOGFGK9Sk5IazgU3JbZZi7kA1pOs3McLYia4DaJXYpLQOxDBMxirJBoGOSkztr0ihHLj5d3xham08G6-PUq7M-geDhcFy33d75lAzBgsG_swMloqqYUze1fNv65-ZXsjvw5TMKWRyyMuBvJp59fKSnufFKXPrY0ZeIs-0Bwo7g8Uk_nhA_2NWf1i_REuO9V-_1Bnxzt8xXU3S7rrJe8pTBeynIf-vcPmvlV8a_gYAAP__C9qRpA), the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz without tolls, and U.S. sanctions waivers allowing Iran to sell oil freely. American forces would remain in the region during the 60-day window. Trump administration officials say Iran has agreed to dispose of its highly enriched uranium stockpile, but [a senior Iranian source](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGynSAURb8GOxw8ovgKijR2N21KhwtHOQmCA3gd_z5jivzAq_fMmrXXr9fyMhQobj_NjrquaYl4lYC1Yl4om3igsejQhB33lMkEZ267gICRi4HDsDhD4V5k4_SKCNg3qDulvpTop0k2Xve9khNIKfrxy1kYoRvfOL2FGp1yQw8N6YcmBhg60XUA7SRWpawDIeVo7KSYFOioptz-ThSrxzXc6YO5tWlvgva1HoX1PxjMDObrutqMZ8Vcnp3B_D4LRSyFwYwR83YzmJ9n3JvCY6rcbBnRcW-i4w-Xe9p8uDnGTNaj42c2kc6dl5rsn4MC8oKRUuYPhkzk_3NIBnOTtTsuCoHK-Lhvu6Hwz7V-K_BHw98AAAD__x8Wj-k) said that no such agreement exists and that nuclear issues are not part of the current deal. On Sunday, Trump wrote on Truth Social that he had instructed his team [not to rush the deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1qwzAUBeCnsbYE6ep_0FAo3tKp0NHcWteximwZWUnw2xf3FbqeA9-B83UbbphyWu8fuFBoUxlWeu2ZWqM6pIrrRjhSJMwLLaUmzBGPcQAO5sL1BfQQMeVjUCyGiQhIMgrCWm-5dE6xOUhC960seCW0jzJqHsFNmpRRxqtoWQqnxjVowYUAuDo-WTtG4EoZHJ3tFKeYWqnXn5LWNtOUj_Kkeh3LwnKYW9v2Tr510HfQt_po817GhPnsz1DxSpjfy4o5ftbHsnXQb2Vvewe9EMaA9xq8lZILaxyrIW6vlHPazTl9XzD9Uaz9659ngN8AAAD__24Qdlk), adding that "time is on our side." A senior Trump official told the press the deal was [not expected to be signed Sunday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb_GdEFmjIEULqIXIb0iKd7Taks02EMyWYORsSBp9ttX5Be2mpGOdHXu_bx0F2TP0-2KI5k0hG6ibfGUEsWOI04zoSVH6EcaQ2T0Dl-2AwnVQeoD6M4h-1dXZs4MREAqI1PU9bGWqmnK7G6spLIoCKnBpu4r56TuK6mOUFa91k5nbPY0qUEXsigA8kYOdW0dyLKs0Da1KCU5TiHmj8BTutPgX2GlmNswZt7cU5oXoU4CWgHttm1539udCWj3MgJazysJaO3tawb9BDU_kgAl1OlbqFOiZxLqfA0CNMiP__s5_404CfgThoEto3-jRN4v7-8fruzyLBo3b-w9L9UueRuR_Vsq_WrJ1cBPAAAA__9mjoNq) and would take several days to move through approvals.
## Russia Hits Kyiv with Massive Missile Barrage
Russia launched [one of the war's largest aerial assaults](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4zwAxu7oIgUWUqxaVNab-F552UwjICdFfn6yPmF1Ee6Ovf8etvfkCOnj594kmtH3hN91UitUdm5YHoSegqE8aQzF8YYsPsdFMxSTRKmPSDHvpshuIMISA_kRmtXq_SymOHuVjLH7Nf1Yiv4ZfTvs8Ewr2OwkyU1sLvW1ATTqMYR4Laow1ofQBkzo1-sMIoCt1xuvzOndqcj9vyicvP5HKK7t_asQn8TsAnY8N1fDy4mYPuRGpWEjXPCKGArn7Uyyoifyd-pykovKiQDYYhdnlwrR5LYGvqHfHR-yT8UKdVH7wK22nLpQm8chP4-ag2zXpQZigvPL46R63y5fpzI8Z9b-6-gLwd_AwAA__-KaYtH) on Ukraine overnight Sunday, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones in a strike that killed at least four people and injured 83. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv was the primary target. Among the weapons used was the Oreshnik, [a nuclear-capable hypersonic ballistic missile](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O2zAQRE8jdTRWS1EkCxZp3DltSmFNruyNqR9QtA3dPlCu8JWDAQZv3p_beCPJsjx-08yhTuu48HfPXCuXUQotG1PkxJRnntcilBMdcUTAQYFRaMZEko-xb1OYmJF1y6Gz1lvQzvXtM_QaDHSoB4igtWMi0Kg1aO_IM5hWwrkGBk0HXYd4cTBZGxNC3w8UnW164CR1LZe_qyz1yVM-1g-XS1znNodnrdve6F8NXhu80nYeOKszlCoxc4PX8t53IfV-FZKF1ZeKeh3yUbPsu2RWqawLK6qV4kt574iJ7sZpHUl7ix6SZ0ar7R3YtCWk7Ss5yz6cdI-ZJP-nqT9S-An4LwAA__-fn4NX) that reportedly flies at more than 10 times the speed of sound. Sunday's launch marked only the third combat use of the system in the war. [Residential buildings, a school, a water supply facility](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOrDAQRE8D2SC7MTYEDn5CNj_dEDV2M9OrBiNjDeL2K_YKm5VU0ivV-3pOT2Th7fUfV_JlSdNG5yFUCuWJM247YaBIKCutKTNKxCtMoMA-VPeAborIck2mjn4hAmpr8tq5wam270399rafh1aTAbOoodMBMDhjZ4OzG1DZuWZ_01QHnVZaAzS9WpwLEZQxFkPvKqMockm5-U68lTctcqUP5SaktRb_LmU_qvZfBWMF43mezTyHu6tgvM9UMGIuHITuGOTabd_qa-9SnX3cTxbhw94rrxVZfqnlTyo-Hn4CAAD__8-lcU4), and the Chernobyl Museum in Kyiv were among the damaged sites. Ukraine's interior minister called the museum strike "a deliberate attack on history, memory, and truth." Russia said the assault was retaliation for a Ukrainian drone attack on a student dormitory in Russian-occupied Starobilsk, which Kyiv denies. European leaders condemned the strike, and [Poland scrambled fighter jets](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L9ugzAQx_GngY3ouJhABg9d2NK1o3Wxz8k1_oOMS8TbV_QVuv_0_Ui_r5u5kQRJj0-KrKvPJvF7DVwrFyOF0sJk2TGFyDEXoeBotwYBLx0MHQ7GkYTdqNZpz4x8bln343gd4TxNqn3qOw2WyQGjvQNe7dRfvec7DkCslIdW9FGDAYce-h7xNIEfR-sQlLqQncZGATupuZy-s6T6ZB_2vHE52RzboJ-1Lmtz_mhwbnB-7bJJcrxwcpzqsWlwLj_rKpQ6qpXsq4u0d6i6w21wbot2y1tCkPVyYI9IEv7i9V-PbBp_AwAA__8j_nTX) in response.
## Memorial Day Cookouts Cost More This Year
Americans firing up the grill this Memorial Day are paying noticeably more for backyard staples, with [ground beef prices up 14.5% and steak up 16.1%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1yhCAUx0-jHQ6iqFtQpLHbtCmdJzwXEuDtAK7x9hkzkxOk_3_-Pu7LHZx38fEOAVXZaIl4ZI-lYFpcgvhE0GgQfMBAyYE3cOpFcDEwLpmQiwHnz6WvjdoQBXY1qnYcbyPvpqmvrdKdkf0AurvpoW_XAaRsYTAdb6FDva61U1cal0K2vG2FaCa-jaM2gveXbxqrnqNxhVLzSS4Wi5s_6YWp0RRqr2wpz1x1b5WYKzEfx9Fs9L3u2UXM-dJUYkZNkcJZidlSLi4-2N8dZuBkmuiL9sIsJszM0sHCri3TtHvDNOVSJ2Weh_Pe5eHa8wjg_G9_-Re0lxI_AQAA__-ewINt) year over year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' April inflation report. The beef squeeze traces to a [U.S. cattle herd at its lowest level in 75 years](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTSB0FiqJEumDxGnd-bUphzV3Zm_DHIAkL8ukDB8gJUk4zH2Y-LusFOHC6_YdIrm15TbTXQK1RWblAehB4QoIQKebCEBAOvyqpFiFnoeYVgcOx6h7dRqRo6smNxpyMnKzV_d3ZSU6krZ_JLyd9nZcFN2uuCNJqjwQ9u3ebnNU8ynFUarByM8ajklov4K3ptCTklsvwmTm1O23hyE8qg8-xD-7e2qN2079OnTt13vd92K5DLrdOnSOUL2qCU6PwjgRNIEVIKCq_XoGqgCp-lwmEQySCUvvi8LFzCFyXN3-LwOGHa3_66OnUdwAAAP__nS18UQ), as ranchers cut inventory amid drought, high feed costs, and rising overhead. Hot dogs aren't a free pass either, with [frankfurter prices up 10.7%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAQRb8Gd3SwROEtWMzG3ZvtLE0JpTKNYIDujn8_0WS-4O2qUjcnde6f7-kbffBx_Y07mbqkKdKnBKqV8uQzxoPQkiMMO-0pewwOTzuBgIGLnkM_OfThnGTjzEIE1DVkWqW-lOi0ls1mNIkvq9HOzs3KSTGARkuy63o9z9jJxpuLJnroW9G2AA8tFqWsAyHlgFYrJgU5X1N-_E0-1o2WcKY35YdNexPMVutRWPeLwchgBKk-GEKp15XBeFAuKWLgi48YLV0RAQODUfR3nMH4X407PLlN6ZleldtUauGYidv8KpuPK7_AVAufiRb-OngreamEz3se-JYqd2kt99oyGJts3PHxIfgyXBbrjj7cX9cfVf028C8AAP__VSmR1w) from last year, and even cakes and cookies climbing 5.1%. The one bright spot for budget-conscious hosts: chicken is the only protein category that got cheaper, down 0.7% over the last year, while potatoes are about 3% less expensive.

A senior Trump official told the press the deal was and would take several days to move through approvals. Russia Hits Kyiv with Massive Missile Barrage Russia launched on Ukraine overnight Sunday, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones in a strike that killed at least four people and injured 83. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv was the primary target. Among the weapons used was the Oreshnik, that reportedly flies at more than 10 times the speed of sound. Sunday's launch marked only the third combat use of the system in the war. , and the Chernobyl Museum in Kyiv were among the damaged sites. Ukraine's interior minister called the museum strike "a deliberate attack on history, memory, and truth." Russia said the assault was retaliation for a Ukrainian drone attack on a student dormitory in Russian-occupied Starobilsk, which Kyiv denies. European leaders condemned the strike, and in response. Memorial Day Cookouts Cost More This Year Americans firing up the grill this Memorial Day are paying noticeably more for backyard staples, with year over year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' April inflation report. The beef squeeze traces to a , as ranchers cut inventory amid drought, high feed costs, and rising overhead. Hot dogs aren't a free pass either, with from last year, and even cakes and cookies climbing 5.1%. The one bright spot for budget-conscious hosts: chicken is the only protein category that got cheaper, down 0.7% over the last year, while potatoes are about 3% less expensive. ## Cornyn Won't Commit to Backing Paxton
Sen. John Cornyn on Sunday [declined to say whether he would support](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ_GdETDYONQuNiGLttuiQY8BEv-k_Em4e2vyCvc-hx9R-f795gf5LyLz78U2NTPlubI78NzrVzmnXI-A4dUHHlL51ZSqDtXnhFwaEG1qGZLzp-zbKxZwI5dw6bTetSgQfbNbuAuNeDSo7I9y22DZdUKbS_BEg_23jhzwUCh6jqQ0N2WUQ0DdNxZGrVcSUhg62oqt-_2h47Nn-nF5bam0Hiz15oP0f8ROAmc6s678_7KBE57CnwdEjitFDK5ZxQ4qfvY4yjbWv6H3HK0qRwcONZ2TSWesc30qelqNsXY_Hbeu2PQQsIzkPuym_o7Wy-DPwEAAP__jzJ_hQ) Trump-endorsed Ken Paxton if the Texas attorney general wins their upcoming GOP Senate runoff. Cornyn said he expects to win the nomination and called the question speculative. Trump endorsed Paxton last week, praising him as a "true MAGA Warrior" while describing Cornyn as a "good man" who was late to back him. The runoff has [drawn comparisons to the primary defeats](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3SoyAYha9GOxxAFCkotkmXbbd03sBLZJYfB0iMd_-NuYWvOs2Z5_z8u6938MGn51-IqNvH5TXhUQO2hmXdYN_PiDEXD8HC6UqObcOGK6d8JnQifFot-HCuorf6Qa1iPWompZJUUjH2m14eZpZMjYsRUoFDubhxHunipHAUzNh7fcHoxCfGqKBseKhpnilDZkFJYaATFK1vuQzf7A9UF878xjKYHPugt9b22o1_On7r-O04juGacCD-vwwdv5lc0pnIDp-WE_kSSMUEDUl5pewciVCrR2IusSdp5RV3YnJqBWojjKll4Xzui7b74UPwdZadoM8IPnxLtN9d99b8JwAA__8h54WL) of Sen. Bill Cassidy and Rep. Thomas Massie, both of whom lost to Trump-backed challengers. Cornyn said his situation is different. Election Day for the primary runoff is this Tuesday. The winner will face Democrat James Talarico in November.
## Carry the Load Honors the Fallen
Several hundred people [walked a three-mile loop through Trinity Park](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upCAUx58GOwwgylhQbGN3t93SHOEwkCAYIOP49ht9hduek9__69_P-gMhhvT-Czvq9nV5TXjWiK1hWT0cx7XjnkuAaOFyJe_NY8NVMDFRNlIxrhZCvFbZWb0xO_MONVdqVkwxOXReDyO8XoYb5caXNIoNg3POGDlsbOLzhF3Qtxgbxcg5k4z32zxOE-PILcxKGiCSoQ0tl_7x_kJ18cofLL3Jexe1b-2oZPhDxELEcp5nb7Z6t7j_RCwPQsRyn4hYDJRy0eaRxgyW-pxyqdRBjJiox5Kx0pCoy6XRM5fmqYUYoVJIloIpudaHTtBCTkQsXdH2OEOMoU6KSPbeIcQnW_vdoh8t_gcAAP__V6GN0g) in Fort Worth on Saturday as part of Carry the Load, a national event honoring fallen service members and first responders. Our remembrance. | | | [CLICK HERE TO LEARN MORE ABOUT KEVIN FORD JR](https://z6h1.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a142cccf19ce44a66365ccd&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fmeetkford%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D69f2afdb5a8a1268a83b8431%26ss_email_id%3D6a142cccf19ce44a66365ccd%26ss_campaign_name%3DRemembering%2BOur%2BFallen%2BHeroes%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2026-05-25T11%253A04%253A48Z&w=67e59626f08d7b1924bf5048&c=b_69f2afdb5a8a1268a83b8431&l=en-US&s=75E3MjV8zhbiJ8VA6L6TcJ759d0%3D)

#### Today, we pause to honor the men and women who gave their lives in service to this country.
#### Maryland has a long and proud connection to military service. From communities across our state, generations of service members answered the call and carried the responsibility of defending both our nation and the people they loved back home.
#### Memorial Day is not simply about ceremony. It is about remembering the cost of sacrifice and recognizing the families who continue to carry that loss every day.
#### This Memorial Day, we honor the brave Americans who gave their lives in service to our nation. May we never forget their sacrifice, and may we continue the work of supporting the veterans, families, and communities they fought to protect.
#### As we spend time with loved ones this weekend, I hope we also take a moment to reflect on those who never had the opportunity to return home.
#### To every military family in District 24 and across Maryland, we honor and remember your sacrifice.
#### Wishing you a safe and meaningful Memorial Day.
#### Kevin Ford, Jr.

name: Molly Gray
subject: This Memorial Day
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Peter,
This morning I’ll be marching in parades in Middlebury in Vergennes. While it is always special to me to see kiddos and families out in community enjoying local traditions, I am reminded that today is about our brave Vermonters who paid the ultimate price in service to our country.
Today, and every day, we honor their memory with profound gratitude.
Today, I will also be thinking about the families left behind — the spouses, children, parents, and loved ones who carry both pride and heartbreak.
Memorial Day is not only about remembering those we lost, but also recognizing the incredible strength, and sacrifice, of Vermont’s Gold Star families.
To the family and friends of Vermont’s fallen heroes: I am holding you in my heart today.
Separately, as many may know, many Vermonters have deployed in recent months with the Vermont National Guard or Air Guard. While we gather for community events, please remember that there are Vermont Guard families across Vermont navigating hardship and uncertainty.
If you know a Guard family, please consider delivering a warm meal, offering to mow a lawn, or help with child care. You can also learn more about Vermont Guard programs and services for families here [https://www.ngfamily.vt.gov/] .
Wishing you a safe, meaningful and reflective Memorial Day.
My very best,
Molly Gray

There's a lot going on out there, as usual. But I want to spotlight a solution that I think would make a huge difference in millions of people's lives that is achievable right now without legislation. What is it?
A four-day workweek.
In early 2025, I got an email asking, "Do you want to be interviewed for a book about a 4-day workweek?"
"Sure," I said. This was a topic that I was very fond of.
The book is now out. I interview the authors of "Do More In Four: Why It's Time for a Shorter Workweek" Joe O'Connor and Jared Lindzon on the podcast this week. I advocated for a 4-day workweek during my presidential campaign in 2020. I believe a shorter workweek would enable us to benefit from AI's ability to do more and would also preserve a few jobs at the margins. It would also preserve our health, our mental health, our time, and our relationships.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/29332f9b-340b-4273-b772-1f3084a35425?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Right now, it feels like we're working harder and harder. Meanwhile, Keynes predicted years ago a 15-hour workweek because our productivity would be so high and techies like Bill Gates have recently predicted the same.
"Work expands or shrinks to fill the time you allocate to it," Joe observes. "This has become known as 'Parkinson's Law' after someone who lived this rule in her own life."
Most of us have experienced this - if we have to get something done in a couple days, we get it done. If we're given five days for the same task . . . it somehow takes us to the end of the period.
"Numerous studies with dozens of companies have found that we get the same amount of work done in 4 days as we do in 5," Joe states. Most of us have experienced this too. If we're going on vacation for a weekend, we work harder to make sure we get our stuff done so we can leave on time and relax.
"There's nothing magical about a 5-day workweek," Jared points out. "It originated during the Industrial Revolution and Henry Ford. People actually thought a forty-hour workweek would ruin the nation's work ethic because previously, people worked much longer hours at factories. That obviously didn't happen. But this industrial setup has essentially lasted a hundred years till today. Now, with AI and knowledge work, our jobs are vastly different but we are still adhering to the same schedule."
Joe's company, Work Time Revolution, helps companies make the transition. "41 American companies adopted a 4-day workweek as a pilot, and the vast majority of them elected to keep it after six months. They saw an average increase in company revenue of 15% per year, as well as a marked improvement in morale and retention." Early adopter companies will have a real advantage in keeping the best people; who would want to go from a 4-day workweek back to a five day?
Joe and Jared believe that this is the path to change - "Historically, a change like this has been made in the private sector by organizations, not through legislation. If anything, the legislation follows after it's already been adopted by companies."
As you'd imagine, this made me think about my own company, Noble Mobile. We're less than a year-old and still need to work hard and grow. But years from now, would I like to see us adopt a 4-day workweek? I'm sure the team would enjoy it, and I've always believed in investing in talent and morale. This is, fundamentally, a different way to invest in people that most companies can afford.
Joe and Jared are thinking big. "A four-day workweek is better for the environment. It benefits our mental health, our physical health, our stress levels, our creativity, our relationships and our productivity. It could even encourage people to have children since they'd be able to spend more time with their families, as there are numerous findings that parents distribute more responsibilities when they have another day at home." Imagine if every weekend was a 3-day weekend. That's a change that most of us could get behind.

I think we need to be honest about something.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ae53afc-a556-4c91-9b06-c6bbd8dca8f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Establishment Democratic liberals are conservative. Not conservative in the MAGA sense. Not conservative in the evangelical, Reaganite, right-wing Republican sense.
I am talking about conservatism in the institutional sense.
Conservatism, broadly understood, is about preserving existing institutions, protecting inherited systems, favoring gradual change, and resisting disruption. That does not only exist on the right. That absolutely exists inside the Democratic Party too.
A lot of modern establishment Democratic liberalism says it is culturally progressive. It says supports diversity, tolerance, climate language, housing language, equity language, and democracy language.

But in fact it is institutionally conservative. When the actual solution requires building, changing, challenging incumbents, disrupting donors, reforming zoning, questioning institutions, or moving faster than the system is comfortable with, the instinct becomes conservative.
Protect the process. Protect the institution. Protect local control. Protect the incumbent. Protect the donor structure. Protect the old way of doing things.
Status-quo bitches.
[Share The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/redirect/c29c73b0-c61e-431d-90c3-dc4b83adbfc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Conservatism Is Not Just Republicanism
This is where the conversation has to start. If we define conservatism only as Republican politics, then we miss what is happening inside our own party.
The Republican Party has become reactionary. It wants to drag the country backward. But the Democratic establishment has become preservationist. It does not usually want to reverse social change. It wants to manage the current system more politely and with better language.
But preserving a broken system is still a form of conservatism.
That is the distinction. The Republican Party is reactionary. The Democratic establishment is preservationist. And preservationism is a form of conservatism.
You can see it in housing. You can see it in transportation. You can see it in clean energy. You can see it in technology. You can see it in the way the party protects incumbents. You can see it in the way the DNC handles accountability. You can see it whenever reform challenges the people already holding power.
The Democratic establishment says it wants change.
But too often, it fights like hell to block it.
* * *
### Housing Is the Cleanest Example
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8eed161e-7b2b-48a9-b3a4-ac84de3f1492?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Friend's Picture of Japanese Housing Zoning
Democrats talk about housing affordability all the time. Housing is too expensive. Rent is too high. Young people cannot buy homes. Working families are getting pushed out. Homelessness is a crisis. Climate change requires density and transit-oriented development.
Talking points.
But when housing reform actually challenges zoning, wealthy neighborhoods, local control, and the ability of existing homeowners to veto new development, a lot of Democratic liberals suddenly sound like old-school conservatives.
California is probably the clearest example. [Governor Gavin Newsom](https://substack.com/redirect/18e5ce29-d7af-4f97-90d7-f79efdff32a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) signed SB 79 in 2025, a law meant to allow denser housing near major transit stops. It is basic climate and housing logic: build more homes near trains and buses. But Los Angeles leaders, including Mayor Karen Bass and members of the City Council, opposed it over local control and community input concerns.
[Then in 2026, seven California Senate Democrats joined Republicans to oppose Scott Wiener's SB 677](https://substack.com/redirect/4a6eb9d1-649d-4046-a34b-ccce7c7a07c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which was designed to close a loophole cities were using to avoid building more housing near transit.
That is liberal conservatism.
New York had a similar problem. Governor Kathy Hochul proposed the N[ew York Housing Compact to build 800,000 homes over a decade](https://substack.com/redirect/1857ab3c-2333-4bde-827d-8737e4918076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but after suburban and local opposition, she backed away from mandatory housing growth requirements.
Democrats say housing is a human right until the solution requires overriding wealthy suburbs, zoning boards, and the politics of "community character."
* * *
### "Local Control" Is Often Just Liberal "States' Rights"
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..92TJiUuJb5eA7-WVNc4QIFm1kcGK68_KBP5uTSXL_KE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199083990)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..92TJiUuJb5eA7-WVNc4QIFm1kcGK68_KBP5uTSXL_KE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199083990)
Local control sounds democratic. It sounds participatory. It sounds like community input. But in practice, local control often gives veto power to the already housed, already wealthy, already organized, and already powerful.
It becomes the liberal version of states' rights.
It is a phrase that sounds neutral while protecting the status quo. It lets people say they support reform in theory while blocking reform in practice.
Housing? Local control.
Transit? Local control.
Solar farms? Local control.
Wind turbines? Local control.
Shelters? Local control.
Apartments near transit? Local control.
At some point, local control becomes a polite way to say, "Nothing changes unless the people already benefiting from the current system approve it."
That is conservative.
* * *
### Democrats Want Clean Energy Until Someone Has to Build It
The same thing happens with climate.
Democrats say they believe in clean energy. They say they believe in fighting climate change. They say we need wind, solar, batteries, transmission lines, grid upgrades, and a new energy economy.
But when clean energy becomes a real-world construction project, suddenly the conversation changes.
Now it is about viewsheds. Neighborhood character. Land use. Agriculture. Wildlife. Local process. Developer distrust. Property values. Community input. More studies. More hearings. More delay.
To be clear, some of those concerns are legitimate. Not every project is good. Not every developer should be trusted. Communities should have some say in what happens around them.
But the larger pattern is still there.
[The Sabin Center at Columbia Law School](https://substack.com/redirect/fdb809f6-6c66-4996-b00f-ec04d4d763ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has tracked severe local restrictions on renewable energy projects across the country, and by the end of 2024, it found that hundreds of counties and municipalities had adopted major restrictions on renewables. The opposition is not always simply left versus right. It often comes down to land use, aesthetics, local power, and distrust of the process.
That is what makes this so interesting. Sometimes the conservative farmer wants the solar lease because it brings income and tax revenue, while the liberal process-oriented activist wants to slow the project down.
**So who is actually conservative there?**
The person willing to build the future, or the person trying to preserve the view?
* * *
### Technology Shows the Same
Tech is another place where establishment Democratic liberalism often becomes conservative.
I know, I know. Elon is a polarizing figure. But it is still worth saying that companies like Tesla and Starlink created some tech that directly connect to things Democrats have been having for decades. Electric vehicles. Climate change. Broadband access in rural areas. Infrastructure gaps.
But instead of separating the technology from the person, a lot of Democratic liberals react ideologically. They do not want Elon to win. They do not want Elon to get money. They do not want to be associated with anything he built. People put bumper stickers on Teslas saying they bought the car before they knew Elon was crazy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c8f461d-0263-404a-8020-1e2d0456cc62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But at some point, the question has to be whether we want outcomes or self inflicted ideological purity. If rural Southeast Ohio lacks broadband and Starlink can reach places where cable has failed, do we actually care about connecting people? Politics over people? OR People over Politics?
That is the conservative I am talking about.
Preserve the political comfort zone, even if the tool could solve a problem.
* * *
### Transit Is Where Democratic Cities Expose Themselves
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bddfc269-56ff-4f77-a5ec-e463ddb47c1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.cpreview.org/articles/2024/9/how-honolulus-rail-overpromised-overcharged-and-underdelivered](https://substack.com/redirect/8a86e4c5-32da-48ab-a72a-3cec58daed23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Democratic cities love transit branding.
And if you look at the progress we have had in the past decades, that is only what it is. Transit Branding.
They love talking about walkability, equity, climate, density, and reducing car dependence. They love transit station plans, studies, community meetings, environmental reviews, ribbon cuttings, and big speeches about the future.
But the United States barely builds rail.
In 2024, [American cities added only about 29 kilometers, or roughly 18 miles](https://substack.com/redirect/23ab5378-1ed4-4c36-8946-b21f6d6a647d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), of light rail and no new metro rail service, according to The Transport Politic's year-end roundup. That is **pathetic** for a country and party that claims to care about climate, mobility, and urban affordability.
And we see the same thing locally. Cleveland and Cuyahoga County talk about transportation, but [RTA continues to face major challenges](https://substack.com/redirect/3294b9a6-b817-4158-bc2c-d6baaa22d5fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and we still do not seem to plan around public transit in a serious way. Look at the [Cleveland Browns stadium conversation](https://substack.com/redirect/3f9b5e3a-406f-4dd6-8fdc-1f0aa46681de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Where is the bold transit planning? Where is the actual infrastructure vision? Where is the discipline to say, if we are building or relocating major public assets, transit must be central?
Instead, we get the same slow, managed decline.
Study it. Talk about it. Frame it. Review it. Delay it. Then wonder why nothing changes.
That is not progressivism. That is bait and switch conservatism.

### The Party Protects Itself Too
This is not only about public policy. It is also about the Democratic Party itself.
[The David Hogg fight inside the DNC is one of the clearest examples.](https://substack.com/redirect/887bdc2b-ec1d-4e80-8f47-0251288990b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hogg and Leaders We Deserve announced a $20 million effort to support younger candidates and primary challenges, including challenges to House Democrats in safely Democratic seats. The backlash was immediate. The DNC ultimately moved to redo the vice chair elections, and Hogg announced he would not seek to remain in the role.
You can dress that up however you want. Procedure. Neutrality. Party unity. Avoiding infighting.
But the deeper message was obvious.
Do not challenge incumbents. Do not threaten the internal order. Do not organize against the people already in power.
That is establishment protectionism. That is institutional conservatism.

The establishment does not just disagree with progressives. It treats them as a threat to the order of the party. When younger candidates, left candidates, working-class candidates, anti-corporate candidates, or grassroots candidates challenge the old structure, the reaction is often not debate. It is containment.
And this is not just one race. Progressive challengers are showing up across the country, and when they win, it is treated as a shock to the system instead of evidence that voters may actually want a different kind of politics.
That is why this fits the larger argument. The Democratic establishment says it wants democracy, but too often it wants democratic managerialism. It wants participation, but only if participation but only their way. It wants energy, but only if that energy can be controlled. It wants younger voters, working-class voters, and disillusioned voters, but it does not always want the candidates those voters actually produce.
**They just want the money and free volunteer labor.**
I already wrote about the DNC autopsy report as a leadership issue, and I'll link to that here. But the deeper pattern is the same. The institution's first instinct is often self-protection.
Again, that is not progress.
That is preservation.

* * *
### The Establishment Liberals Are Not the Party of Change
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..92TJiUuJb5eA7-WVNc4QIFm1kcGK68_KBP5uTSXL_KE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199083990)
This is the core of it.
The modern Democratic establishment has become conservative in practice, even while remaining liberal in branding. It conserves institutions, incumbents, zoning systems, donor relationships, seniority, process, regulatory structures, and procedural norms.
It calls this pragmatism. But for people dealing with housing costs, health care costs, corruption, climate collapse, broken infrastructure, student debt, unaffordable cities, rural decline, corporate power, and democratic backsliding, it looks like managed decline.
When every solution dies in process, that is **conservatism**.
When every reform gets watered down or financially bloated to protect stakeholders, that is **conservatism**.
When every new idea gets buried under studies, task forces, and local veto points, that is **conservatism**.
When new candidates are treated as threats, that is **conservatism**.
When the party protects incumbents before voters, that is **conservatism**.
When we talk about the future but preserve the present, that is **conservatism**.
* * *
### The Solution
The Democratic Party needs to stop with the bull shit.
We need to build or allow housing, not just talk about affordability.
We need to build or allow clean energy, not just talk about climate.
We need to build or allow transit, not just talk about equity.
We need to allow primary challenges, not treat them like attacks on democracy.
We need to hold party leadership accountable, not hide behind process every time someone asks hard questions.
The Democratic Party **can still** be the party of the future. But...
Establishment Democratic liberalism has become... weak AF.
It has become too comfortable preserving institutions that are not delivering results.
It has become too comfortable saying the right things while defending systems that prevent those things from happening.
And I think it is time we say that honestly.
The Republican Party is reactionary.
The Democratic establishment is preservationist.
And preservationism is a form of conservatism.

| Dear Peter,
This Memorial Day, we honor the brave Americans who gave their lives defending our nation and protecting the freedoms we cherish.
Their sacrifice reminds us that liberty is never free. May we always remember their courage, their selfless service, and the families who carry their legacy forward with pride and strength.
Today, I had the privilege of taking part in the Pompano Beach Memorial Day Parade, where our community came together in solemn remembrance of the heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country. It was a meaningful tribute to their bravery, patriotism, and enduring legacy. A special thank you to the elected officials and organizers in Pompano Beach for hosting such a heartfelt and respectful remembrance event.
On this Memorial Day, let us pause to reflect, honor, and express our deepest gratitude to those who gave everything in service to the United States of America.

clean_body: | | | | | == | AMERICA FIRST. NAVY VETERAN. PROVEN LEADER. | Dear Peter, This Memorial Day, we honor the brave Americans who gave their lives defending our nation and protecting the freedoms we cherish. Their sacrifice reminds us that liberty is never free. May we always remember their courage, their selfless service, and the families who carry their legacy forward with pride and strength. Today, I had the privilege of taking part in the Pompano Beach Memorial Day Parade, where our community came together in solemn remembrance of the heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country. It was a meaningful tribute to their bravery, patriotism, and enduring legacy. A special thank you to the elected officials and organizers in Pompano Beach for hosting such a heartfelt and respectful remembrance event. Sound of FreedomTwo young sisters were rescued from trafficking. Your gift helps protect vulnerable children from unimaginable evil. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE

Friend,

My heart is heavy as I write this.

Two little sisters in Uganda, ages 13 and 9, were found shaking in silence behind a locked door.

Their eyes were hollow. Their voices had gone quiet long before rescuers arrived.

It started with something that could happen in almost any family.

An argument at home.
The girls ran away scared and alone.

Then a man appeared and offered to help. For a moment, it probably felt like an answer to prayer.

Instead, it was a trap.
He locked them in a room for days.
No way out - just fear and the crushing thought that no one was coming.

But someone did come.

A local worker heard suspicious noises and called the police.

Then a Sound of Freedom Foundation rescue partner was contacted to help.

If you’ve never heard of us before, the Sound of Freedom Foundation is a faith-driven movement.

We're dedicated to stopping the sale of God’s children and helping protect vulnerable children from trafficking and exploitation.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODd9AAwAAAAAANOtCHYGjgYBZx0jUTxA1mFqCOIiAvnKeqvVCBYwdFgCt8IKaNpWsXpH7bMFTFxk5dzrv60OAWYBFnhcsR1f_oanVcQgqaqTvcB4q3F4mw
Give Now to Protect God’s Children

My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

After years of working alongside rescuers and hearing firsthand what trafficked children endure, our mission grew out of the Sound of Freedom film I produced.

Because supporters stepped forward, trained responders were ready when these girls needed help most.

Police broke down the door and the suspect was arrested.

And while officers secured the scene, a social worker knelt beside those frightened girls and whispered:

“You are safe now.”
“You are not alone.”

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODd9AAwAAAAAANOtCHYHLwCjw3d_83v2yWuiZOku_8mP7zDGyr4OZ0J09cpq7yL3717SLPV6ApTr5y2ydnG009KyyPaoNjl2SrsXqQ89iVADcbdvzseyGA

Friend, this is what your support makes possible.

Not just rescue, but healing, protection and care.

After children are rescued, the trauma does not disappear overnight.

The two sisters needed medical care, counseling, safe shelter and advocates to help them through police interviews and court proceedings.

They needed a place where they could simply be children again.

And thanks to compassionate people who refused to look away, they received it.

At the Sound of Freedom Foundation, we work to help stop trafficking through five areas of action:

- Prevention to strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children

- Intervention that equips trusted rescue partners to save exploited children

- Education that helpsparents and communities recognize trafficking warning signs

- Information to raise awareness about the growing trafficking crisis

- Influence to advance stronger protections for vulnerable children

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODd9AAwAAAAAANOtCHYIe4ABwARUq5N6FXV2Z3svfp4nWF9yWYQlP_hNKFn1RAtl0hKhzzgA67UVYETIgcKsBliEsw9k5v3oPIpvz3TLE7BZm82avt6gJw
Give Now to Protect God’s Children

Jesus said:

“Let the little children come to me… for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” (Matthew 19:14)

We believe every child is made in the image of God.
Precious and worthy of protection.

God’s children are not for sale.

Today, I’m asking you not to look away.

Will you make your first gift to help protect vulnerable children and support rescue and aftercare efforts for survivors?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODd9AAwAAAAAANOtCHYJ4-AKyBS24rC5Fnx0wluJAmje5oFHII64D8UA5rvEOmfdzy2lELZylMfRKJft5ievQsm2vuWftxuZQCoF7sd1NxnQSKdi4hRkEg
Friend, will you give $25, $50, $100, or whatever God places on your heart today?

Your gift can directly help provide:

- Emergency response support
- Safe shelter and counseling
- Medical care and trauma recovery
- Family support and protection services
- Education and prevention efforts for at-risk communities

The truth is hard to face, but together, we can help bring light into very dark places.

And we can remind frightened children they are not forgotten.

With gratitude and prayer,

Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer

clean_body: View in browser A Special Message from our SponsorPlease note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Parler and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Parler. Sound of FreedomTwo young sisters were rescued from trafficking. Your gift helps protect vulnerable children from unimaginable evil. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE Friend, My heart is heavy as I write this. Two little sisters in Uganda, ages 13 and 9, were found shaking in silence behind a locked door. Their eyes were hollow. Their voices had gone quiet long before rescuers arrived. It started with something that could happen in almost any family. An argument at home. The girls ran away scared and alone. Then a man appeared and offered to help. For a moment, it probably felt like an answer to prayer. Instead, it was a trap. He locked them in a room for days. No way out - just fear and the crushing thought that no one was coming. But someone did come. A local worker heard suspicious noises and called the police. Then a Sound of Freedom Foundation rescue partner was contacted to help. If you’ve never heard of us before, the Sound of Freedom Foundation is a faith-driven movement. We're dedicated to stopping the sale of God’s children and helping protect vulnerable children from trafficking and exploitation. Give Now to Protect God’s Children My name is Eduardo Verástegui. After years of working alongside rescuers and hearing firsthand what trafficked children endure, our mission grew out of the Sound of Freedom film I produced. Because supporters stepped forward, trained responders were ready when these girls needed help most. Police broke down the door and the suspect was arrested. And while officers secured the scene, a social worker knelt beside those frightened girls and whispered: “You are safe now.” “You are not alone.” Friend, this is what your support makes possible. Not just rescue, but healing, protection and care. After children are rescued, the trauma does not disappear overnight. The two sisters needed medical care, counseling, safe shelter and advocates to help them through police interviews and court proceedings. They needed a place where they could simply be children again. And thanks to compassionate people who refused to look away, they received it. At the Sound of Freedom Foundation, we work to help stop trafficking through five areas of action: - Prevention to strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children - Intervention that equips trusted rescue partners to save exploited children - Education that helpsparents and communities recognize trafficking warning signs - Information to raise awareness about the growing trafficking crisis - Influence to advance stronger protections for vulnerable children Give Now to Protect God’s Children Jesus said: “Let the little children come to me… for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” (Matthew 19:14) We believe every child is made in the image of God. Precious and worthy of protection. God’s children are not for sale. Today, I’m asking you not to look away. Will you make your first gift to help protect vulnerable children and support rescue and aftercare efforts for survivors? Friend, will you give $25, $50, $100, or whatever God places on your heart today? Your gift can directly help provide: - Emergency response support - Safe shelter and counseling - Medical care and trauma recovery - Family support and protection services - Education and prevention efforts for at-risk communities The truth is hard to face, but together, we can help bring light into very dark places. And we can remind frightened children they are not forgotten. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verástegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. name: Wes Moore
subject: Honoring those who gave their lives for this country
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1413%2E1086043%2ERL1uti)
Peter, I currently serve as the Governor of Maryland. But I got my start in service in the military — I’m an Army guy.
My military service taught me a lot. To put the safety of others over my own, to live “Mission First, People Always,” and to Leave No One Behind.
To me, that’s true patriotism. Believing that the people around you — your fellow soldiers, your neighbors, and your community — deserve support no matter what. Those are the same values that drive my work as governor. I do not take a single day for granted representing Maryland.
When I was deployed to Afghanistan as a member of the 82nd Airborne Division of the Army, I was honored to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with some of the best soldiers in the world. It forged the strongest friendships I have ever experienced.
But unfortunately, not all of my brothers and sisters made it home. There were some who struggled with mental health and lost their lives to the invisible wounds of war when they returned. And I will never forget their sacrifice.
**Today, and every Memorial Day, we must remember and honor the men and women who gave their lives in service to this country. And we must honor them with service of our own.**
Thank you, and may God bless you,
Wes

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
