Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. Each year, the last Monday of May is observed to honor the men and women who died while serving in the United States military. Formerly known as Decoration Day, this tradition originated after the Civil War and became a federal holiday known as Memorial Day in 1971. Some dispute when the first remembrance occurred, but one of the earliest Memorial Day commemorations on record was organized by a group of former slaves in Charlestown, South Carolina shortly after the Confederacy surrendered in 1865.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=199152103&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5MTUyMTAzLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk3MTY0MzAsImV4cCI6MTc4MjMwODQzMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.rG88ppyjdXPjmNFeb3q0Zu4eRMD5QguSifBKnXu5hZE)
When Decoration Day began in 1865, it honored African American Union Soldiers that had been buried in a Confederate prison camp mass gravesite. The surviving men and women worked diligently to move the bodies of those buried in the mass grave and give each of them proper burials at new gravesites. They decorated their new resting places as a sign of remembrance and respect.
That tradition continues to this day.
On May 30, 1868, thousands gathered at Arlington National Cemetery for the first official Decoration Day ceremony. Before placing flowers or wreaths on the gravesites, then Ohio Congressman James Garfield said, "We do not know one promise these men made, one pledge they gave, one word they spoke; but we do know they summed up and perfected, by one supreme act, the highest virtues of men and citizens." He further stated, "For love of country they accepted death, and thus resolved all doubts, and made immortal their patriotism and their virtue."

Garfield would later become President of the United States, but his words of gratitude that day in Arlington would forever set the tone for honoring those that have asked the least and sacrificed the most. These brave souls understood that true patriotism is a love of country and a true consciousness of its worth. Something that is lost on many in America today.
As we remember and honor the fallen, Memorial Day provides a great opportunity to reflect on the sacrifices made by these heroes. The act of giving up one's life for the greater good is a vital component to the continuation of the American way of life. A soldier's meaning of patriotism is complex and far-reaching, but it's absolute. There's no need to question their intentions or motivations; a simple thank for serving will suffice.
Thank you to all my fellow veterans past and present. You have my utmost gratitude and respect. It has been both an honor and privilege to stand with you.
_May God bless all of you, Vincent_

name: Chris Pappas
subject: Honoring our service members today
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I hope you’ll take a moment today to remember those we’ve lost and to also think about what we owe the people who are still here because of them.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=6825%2E582294%2EtTYRu0)
Team,
On Memorial Day we come together to honor the service members who gave their lives defending our country. It’s a day to reflect on their sacrifice and to think about the responsibility we carry to care for the veterans and military families who are still with us today.
Today we remember the service members throughout our nation’s history who went to war and never came home. The freedoms we have today came at an extraordinary cost.
I grew up hearing stories of service from my grandparents, three of whom served in World War II. My grandfathers were pilots, and my grandmother served in the Coast Guard. Their example shaped how I think about service and what it means to give back.
We’ve been through hard moments as a country before, and we’ve gotten through them because of the people who stepped up and gave their lives in defense of others. That’s something we should never lose sight of.
But today too many veterans are still struggling with basic needs – housing, health care, jobs, and food security. We owe them more than remembrance. We owe them action that actually reflects what they gave for this country.
I hope you’ll take a moment today to remember those we’ve lost and consider what we owe the people who are still here because of them. That’s how we keep the promise we’ve made to every person who wears the uniform.
Wishing you and your family a safe and meaningful Memorial Day.
With appreciation,
Chris

Peter,

This Memorial Day, I want to honor the brave men and women who gave their lives in service to our country. Their sacrifice protected our freedoms and shaped the nation we call home. We owe them, and the families they left behind, our deepest gratitude and enduring support.

Memorial Day is not only a time for remembrance, but also a reminder of our responsibility to care for military families and veterans in meaningful ways. That means ensuring they have access to quality healthcare, stable housing, economic opportunity, and strong community support.

For many surviving military families, programs like the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) remain an essential source of care and stability. As conversations continue nationwide about healthcare access and support for veterans and military families, we must keep their well-being at the center of those discussions.

We should always strive to build communities where military families feel valued, supported, and welcomed. Their sacrifices do not end when service ends, and our commitment to them should not either.

To every military family reading this email: **thank you.** Your sacrifice, resilience, and service to this country deserve recognition not just on Memorial Day, but every day.

Thank you,

Christina

clean_body: | = Peter, This Memorial Day, I want to honor the brave men and women who gave their lives in service to our country. Their sacrifice protected our freedoms and shaped the nation we call home. We owe them, and the families they left behind, our deepest gratitude and enduring support. Memorial Day is not only a time for remembrance, but also a reminder of our responsibility to care for military families and veterans in meaningful ways. That means ensuring they have access to quality healthcare, stable housing, economic opportunity, and strong community support. For many surviving military families, programs like the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) remain an essential source of care and stability. As conversations continue nationwide about healthcare access and support for veterans and military families, we must keep their well-being at the center of those discussions. We should always strive to build communities where military families feel valued, supported, and welcomed. Their sacrifices do not end when service ends, and our commitment to them should not either. To every military family reading this email: thank you. Your sacrifice, resilience, and service to this country deserve recognition not just on Memorial Day, but every day. Thank you, Christina Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. She's running for Congress to defeat Mariannette Miller-Meeks and flip IA-01 blue. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132039815/623202606/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZjM1N2IwNi00MjU4LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htf7AExoxWtF3f3ck-RHmC-n15AJNUE78r2kY9l7fHo=&emci=0cacfd88-5655-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&emdi=6f357b06-4258-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=14565883)

| | For many across the country, this weekend marks the unofficial start of summer — a long weekend filled with backyard barbecues and an endless stream of holiday sales. But for service members, veterans, and military families, the weight of this day carries a completely different meaning. **Memorial Day was never meant to be a casual holiday. It is a day of collective reflection and mourning.** Originally known as Decoration Day, the tradition began just after the Civil War as a dedicated time for communities to pause, close local businesses, and decorate the graves of fallen soldiers. Long before it became a federally recognized holiday in 1966, communities across the country were already gathering to honor those who never returned home. They were gathering to remember brothers, sisters, friends, and loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to a country they loved. They were gathering to honor lives cut short and ensure those sacrifices would never be forgotten. Here in El Paso, we understand that sacrifice in a very personal way. Ours is a community with deep military roots. **For so many of our neighbors, this day isn't just an annual holiday in May — it is a day marked by the quiet absence of those we wish were still here.** When we lose sight of the meaning behind this day, we risk forgetting the weight that military families continue to carry long after the loss itself. For many families, remembrance is not reserved for just one day a year. As you spend time with loved ones this weekend, we hope that you take a moment to look beyond the noise of the commercial holiday and pause to honor the courage and sacrifice of those who never made it home. We wish you and your family a safe and peaceful Memorial Day. subject: Turn America back to Godly values
body:
But now Brave Books has an urgent two-fold problem that I hope you can help with

| | | You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friend in Faith,Please – for the sake of all our families – take it from me as someone who’s lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with “entertainment” that grooms children.You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace.But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue’s Clues_...
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkU2L2zAQhn-NfFOQRl_2wYdkHYdAU0oOLj0JfW1WrC0FW3bpvy8uzQ_Y2_DyzMA878-bvpk4xvT4bqbQui3qedFlnZOZwhydscZ9lvzIfvyzmVEDAYmJwCB2jla-dV4yqEJLlWoUrQVA9dFyKZUQDXACpvbsPXDHjK-J4FzVAmwV2_0SESAop4LKg2is4bJprOVKcKIQJ-vTmxKWg8tpCfNmStxCTCnvU04Hl6dqbD9KeS6IHRH0CPoluHUOB5OCz2UnEPR2NlvANufPBUEPigpwUGMvgsTcco5rKmschFVSBvVeNxSxfi2TXvI6u4BYd-ou-H4eEMg9noKP64RYd779T5yZniY-EmIdEBCEU6JP3UWf7sfhrK-Xyy8Q3_T9POgfR_w2XF9rOZWQCmLd23DFLx_V3Prn7ziOcZG7hcdk4vjv2fL1erYW_gYAAP__c8CW_A)
---
| | Or Sesame Street using YOUR tax-dollars to normalize same-sex parents and men in dresses.And the result is an upside-down world where children lecture YOU about what you can and cannot say... ...and they try to “educate” YOU about your “old-fashioned” and “mean” ideas.Today you have a very special chance to stop the Hollywood groomers who are turning our children and grandchildren against us and the Godly values we love. **[Today, I’m inviting you to be a Founding Supporter of the very first children’s television show that actively fights back against the groomers in Hollywood AND reinforces the traditional biblical values that made America great.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkU2L2zAQhn-NfFOQRl_2wYdkHYdAU0oOLj0JfW1WrC0FW3bpvy8uzQ_Y2_DyzMA878-bvpk4xvT4bqbQui3qedFlnZOZwhydscZ9lvzIfvyzmVEDAYmJwCB2jla-dV4yqEJLlWoUrQVA9dFyKZUQDXACpvbsPXDHjK-J4FzVAmwV2_0SESAop4LKg2is4bJprOVKcKIQJ-vTmxKWg8tpCfNmStxCTCnvU04Hl6dqbD9KeS6IHRH0CPoluHUOB5OCz2UnEPR2NlvANufPBUEPigpwUGMvgsTcco5rKmschFVSBvVeNxSxfi2TXvI6u4BYd-ou-H4eEMg9noKP64RYd779T5yZniY-EmIdEBCEU6JP3UWf7sfhrK-Xyy8Q3_T9POgfR_w2XF9rOZWQCmLd23DFLx_V3Prn7ziOcZG7hcdk4vjv2fL1erYW_gYAAP__c8CW_A)** Introducing: _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_.I’m making this ground-breaking live-action television show with the great folks at **Brave Books**.If you’ve seen me and **Brave Books** on _Fox News_ , you know we’ve already countered those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” the Left has been pushing on children in our taxpayer funded libraries. Thanks to support from parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens just like you, we started hosting Godly and patriotic “Story Hours” of our own.And now, THOUSANDS of children and parents can gather to pledge allegiance to our flag, read wholesome books, and pray together in their libraries.It’s encouraging to see we can win when we fight back! Now we’re working to have that same impact in television.
---
>> Imagine a children's show that leaves your child or grandchild with a greater sense of right and wrong and an understanding of truth.Courage, honesty, discernment, forgiveness, empathy, all taught through a biblical and traditional lens. >> Imagine a children's show that brings families together instead of driving them apart.>> Now imagine YOU are the one who makes that show possible. Because we can’t beat the Hollywood groomers without your help as a **Founding Supporter**.
---
The great news is that we’ve already completed and released the first ten character-building episodes of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_! We premiered it recently to a small group of children and parents and I wish you could have seen the smiles on those innocent little faces.And I wish you could have experienced _the parents_ watching their children absorb the beautiful Gospel messages.It was quite a moment for everyone – including folks just like you – who worked so hard to get us that far. But now **Brave Books** has an urgent two-fold problem that I hope you can help with.
---
_**#1. Brave Books needs to launch a massive advertising blitz to get around the groomers on the Left.**_
---
You see, we’ve made the first five episodes of Season 1 of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ available absolutely FREE. That’s the best way we can reach MILLIONS of families with our Gospel-inspired messaging.But no one will see it if we can’t get the word out. And the Left will try to bury _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ at every turn. The price tag for an advertising blitz of this magnitude is $250,000 – and with the recent launch, we need to raise the funds immediately.
---
_**#2. We must complete Season 2 to keep our momentum going and that cost is $250,000 for post production.**_

Most Mississippians do not know that on July 1, 2025, a little after four o'clock in the morning, the United States Senate voted 99 to 1 to strip a federal AI moratorium out of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
That sounds technical. It was not.
Had that moratorium stayed in the bill, Mississippi could have lost its ability to enforce ordinary state and local rules on the most important industrial development happening in our state.
The danger was real because the provision was real. The House-passed version of the bill contained language imposing a ten-year moratorium on state and local enforcement of laws or regulations "limiting, restricting, or otherwise regulating" artificial intelligence models, artificial intelligence systems, or automated decision systems.
Ten years.
The text was not written as a data-center bill, and that is exactly why it was dangerous. Broad federal language rarely stays narrow once lawyers get hold of it. If an AI data center exists to train, host, or operate AI systems, then companies could argue that state and local rules affecting those facilities are really rules affecting AI. We would have been forced to fight for the right to enforce our own rules on our own soil.
That could have affected Mississippi DEQ. It could have affected county zoning decisions, noise rules, setback requirements, permitting conditions, and environmental reviews if they were challenged as restrictions on AI infrastructure. It could have invited new challenges to utility and grid decisions touching AI data-center loads.
Apply that to what is already happening. The lawsuit over xAI's Southaven gas turbines turns in part on Mississippi DEQ's interpretation of its own temporary-mobile rule. Under a broad reading of the moratorium, xAI or another operator could have argued that state permitting authority over AI-supporting infrastructure was preempted. I want Ai data centers to build in Mississippi, but we need to set the rules not Washington.
What killed the moratorium was a Senate amendment offered by Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee and backed by a bipartisan group. The vote was 99 to 1. Mississippi's two senators, Roger Wicker and Cindy Hyde-Smith, both voted with the 99. Three days later, the President signed the bill without the moratorium in it.
The encouraging part is the margin. When the Senate actually voted on whether states should be shoved aside for ten years on AI regulation, the answer was not close.
The alarming part is that the question almost never got asked.
The provision had already been written, negotiated, tucked into a massive reconciliation package, and passed by the House. It was not in some left-wing bill from California. It was in a Republican-led budget bill supported by an administration most Mississippi conservatives voted for.
That is worth remembering. Government does not only threaten local authority when the other party is in charge. Sometimes it does it with your party's logo on the letterhead.
The federal preemption fight is not over. Senator Ted Cruz, who pushed the moratorium, has made clear the idea is not dead. The technology industry still wants one national rule, and that is easy to understand. One federal rule is cheaper than fifty state fights and easier than convincing county supervisors in DeSoto, Madison, Lauderdale, or anywhere else ordinary people might ask inconvenient questions about water, power, noise, emissions, taxes, and who pays when the deal goes bad.
This is exactly what federalism is for. Mississippi has its own DEQ, Public Service Commission, county supervisors, and city councils so decisions about what gets built next to our neighborhoods are made by people we can call, confront, embarrass, defeat, and replace.
A Senate cloakroom is not local government. A lobbyist-written preemption clause is not economic development. And a thousand-page bill passed in the middle of the night is not self-government.
Throughout this series, I have argued that Mississippi should welcome the data-center boom on its own terms. We should write the rules, enforce them fairly, reject corporate-welfare deals, protect ratepayers, and let the projects stand on their own engineering and balance sheets.
None of that works without local authority.
Mississippi must have the right to say yes. We must have the right to say no. And most importantly, we must have the right to say, "Yes, but not like that."
In July 2025, we almost lost part of that right before most of us even knew the vote was happening. The next attempt is already being telegraphed. This time, Mississippi conservatives should be paying attention before it gets to four in the morning.

# [#]
Peter,

Today, we pause to honor the brave men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our nation. Their courage is the foundation of our democracy, and we owe them a debt of gratitude that can never truly be repaid.

In Rhode Island, we have a long and proud history of service. From the Revolutionary War to the present day, Rhode Islanders have consistently stepped up to defend our nation and our values. As we gather with family and friends today, let us remember that our freedom is not a given; it was earned by those who put their country above themselves.

We owe a tremendous debt to the heroes who walked among us, our neighbors, colleagues, and loved ones who served with distinction. Their stories of valor are woven into the very fabric of our communities, reminding us that the price of liberty is often paid by the few for the benefit of the many.

I am committed to ensuring that we honor their legacy not just with words, but with action. That means fighting for the healthcare and benefits our veterans earned and protecting the democratic institutions they fought to defend.

Please join me today in a moment of silence for our fallen heroes and their families.

— Seth

Friend, Today, we honor and remember the brave Americans who made the ultimate sacrifice for the freedoms and rights we hold sacred. Their courage, service, and selflessness _will never be forgotten._ __ Let’s take a moment to reflect on the extraordinary sacrifice made by military families across Tennessee and our nation, families who carry both pride and loss. Tennesseans know the meaning of service, duty, and love for our country and communities. This Memorial Day, we remember the men and women who gave everything in service of those values. **May we never take their sacrifice for granted.** **From my family to yours, I wish you a safe and meaningful Memorial Day.** With gratitude, **Jerri Green**
Democratic Candidate for Tennessee Governor

subject: Memorial Day message

body:
From a very young age I learned to take a deep breath and brace myself for tears as “Taps” started to play at family funerals and veterans events. Memorial Day is important to our family and I am grateful that my daughters are growing up learning the meaning of the ultimate sacrifice.

Today we pause to remember the men and women from Northeastern Pennsylvania and across our country who gave their own lives in service to our nation. Memorial Day is not a day for politics. It’s a day for gratitude, for family, and for quiet reflection on the cost of our freedoms.

I think of the families who live with that loss every day — parents, spouses, children, friends — and I feel the responsibility that comes with public service. As someone who has spent much of my life working to make government honest and more effective, I know we owe our veterans and their families more than words. We owe them our attention, our respect, and the promise that their sacrifices will not be forgotten.

If you can, please join me in honoring them today: attend a local Memorial Day ceremony, say the names of the fallen out loud, or take a moment of silence with your family. It’s a small act — but it matters.

Thank you for remembering with me.

Paige Cognetti
Mayor, mom, and candidate for Congress

body:
| | | Hey there, it's Marc Elias.

For years, I've gone to court to stop Trump and defend democracy ‐‐ and I've won 64 times. **Now, working with the DSCC, we're doing our part to safeguard voting rights, uphold the rule of law, and protect your freedom.**

But I won't lie: Trump's actions put all that work at risk ‐‐ and we need to fight back NOW. [**Support from grassroots Democrats like you is what powers the fight to flip the Senate so Democrats can put a stop to Trump's extremism. Will you give $7 to the DSCC to help us stop Trump's allies by winning back a Democratic Senate majority?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/23030?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260525-MarcElias-EliasStandingUpToTrump-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260525-MarcElias-EliasStandingUpToTrump-Pros-sl1&akid=23954%2E9716520%2EOX2Mo4)

Let me explain further:

Donald Trump is ignoring due process and openly mocking the courts. He's threatening the very foundation of our democracy by attacking fair, free, and secure elections. And he's going after voting rights ‐‐ the very bedrock of our democracy.

Worst of all, Trump has a seemingly **endless** supply of fools and cowards in the Republican Party who are willing to help him.

But the DSCC and I are fighting back: The _moment_ Trump signed an executive order to interfere in our elections and threaten voting rights last year, we filed suit against him on behalf of Democrats nationwide. And the good news is, we've already notched some key victories in the case!

**But the fight isn't over yet. Donald Trump is an aspiring despot ‐‐ not just for a single day ‐‐ and despots _never_ willingly give up their power. We have to take it from them.**

Winning the Senate is the first step, and Democrats need to flip just four seats to claim the majority and wrest power away from the GOP.

**As I've said before, the fight for democracy is the fight of our generation.[Right now, the best thing YOU can do is chip in $7 to the DSCC to stand in this fight with me to unseat Senate Republicans and elect a Democratic Senate majority the first chance we get >>](https://go.dscc.org/go/23030?amount=7&t=6&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260525-MarcElias-EliasStandingUpToTrump-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260525-MarcElias-EliasStandingUpToTrump-Pros-sl1&akid=23954%2E9716520%2EOX2Mo4)**

body:
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=8193227a143442eb8d3794fc67d21c5c&_e=bkB78nsgDv4Xw-wPYJRPplZOTLJ2L9AiDW6gU-M1xbZUrOGGVutM8OlxruWSc-3AZSXvk8toc58814pacdRtx58hnowDDznFz1IrVs3zjDqdsjLAsmylYLc0e-oYQvs9T6Jtk-yXsyfKtFspiLNVVQG7WOUrnHJrbVAtGPe_oJzBExzbJJ_83fF_S85lcq1AxcUJJx-phQgYo0yTQD-OHtKfAjTmzjzIIL6rL1gcwMn8C74LuNM9vrWsmnp9Jh4hYtyMnKTjHtdeHTJKqS4kmeQyJ2x4zPk2RGomogokT2HdqGYZ9j49pLZ8GgAbgnAQVkIxNXvqxiV-Wke2FmflRfTflSEK5t34rFYOr8gY3D-NFBcflfQ4WuCOGcWo6PxLN4Bf6K5rarwI0xjgYzi0iaK-cjUYt1fu7LDmo6-jO-pCypCStI_NQXZqznxSPt6j) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.
The National Center for Police Defense is standing with Jeff and his family — funding his legal defense and providing support while this ordeal drags on. But we cannot do it without you.

subject: Honoring those who served
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alex Kelloff for Colorado
body:
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
Friend,
Today, we honor the men and women who gave their lives in service to our country.
Memorial Day is a reminder that freedom comes with sacrifice, and that behind every name we remember is a family, a community, and a life dedicated to something bigger than self.
Here in Colorado’s 3rd District, veterans make up 7.8% of our population. Their service continues to shape our communities, and today we also recognize the families who carry the memory of those we’ve lost.
I’ve had the privilege of working alongside members of our military throughout my career, and I’ve seen firsthand the professionalism, courage, and commitment they bring to serving this country.
Today is simply a day to say thank you.
We remember those who served. And we honor the sacrifice they made for all of us.
— Alex Kelloff

subject: Honoring those who gave everything
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jena for Colorado
body:
https://www.jenaforcolorado.com/ [https://www.jenaforcolorado.com/]
Dear Peter,
Today, we honor the brave Americans who gave their lives in service to our country.
Memorial Day is a solemn day to remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice to protect our country, our freedoms, and the democratic values we hold dear.
Across generations, Americans have answered the call to serve, putting something greater than themselves first. We owe an enduring debt to the service members who never made it home, and to the families who continue to carry that sacrifice every day.
As we reflect today, we are also reminded of our responsibility to protect the freedoms and institutions that they fought to defend — the rule of law, free and fair elections, and the rights guaranteed to every American.
Today, may we pause to remember the fallen, honor their sacrifice, and extend our gratitude to the families who continue to carry their legacy forward.
With gratitude,
Jena

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]
Friend,

Memorial Day is a solemn reminder of the profound debt we owe to those who gave everything for our country.

Today isn’t about politics. It is about honoring the courageous service members across Maryland and our District who never made it home, and standing in solidarity with the families who carry their memory every single day.

We are a nation forged and protected by those who step up to serve, but today we pause to remember and respect those who made the ultimate sacrifice.

I hope you can find a moment of peace, reflection, and gratitude with your loved ones today.

Thank you,

Sarah
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/] https://www.facebook.com/SarahforMD [https://www.facebook.com/SarahforMD] https://www.instagram.com/SarahforMaryland [https://www.instagram.com/SarahforMaryland] https://x.com/SarahforMD [https://x.com/SarahforMD]
Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. Peter—Please join me this Memorial Day in honoring and remembering the brave men and women who gave their lives in service to our county.

**Those who made the ultimate sacrifice so that we might live in freedom and peace.**

Countless families in Washington's 8th District carry the legacy of loved ones lost in uniform. Today, we hold those we've lost in our hearts and express our deepest gratitude.

Whether you spend today with family, participating in a community memorial ceremony, or quietly remembering someone you’ve lost, I hope you’ll join me in pausing to reflect on the extraordinary courage and sacrifice of our fallen heroes and what they fought for.

Wishing you and your loved ones a reflective and meaningful Memorial Day.

Warmly,

Kim

subject: on this Memorial Day

Friend, on Memorial Day we acknowledge, reflect, respect, and honor all the U.S. service members who never made it home. They and their families are in my thoughts today and always.
Days like this mean a lot to my family. My dad served in the Marines, and my mom in the Navy. I saw firsthand the dedication, sacrifice, and strength it takes to serve, and I want to say**thank you to every service member and military family across New Mexico. Your courage is unmatched, and we are forever grateful for your service.**
As the daughter of veterans, I’ve always believed we have a responsibility to support the people who serve our country and the families who serve alongside them. Throughout my career, I’ve fought for veterans and military families and honor their sacrifice by making sure they have the support, care, and opportunities they deserve.

****And as New Mexico’s governor, I promise to continue that work and make sure New Mexico is a state that truly supports veterans and military families. We will:****
— Expand rural veteran transportation to all 33 counties
— Hire more Veteran Service Officers
— Help veterans transition into high-paying civilian jobs
— Crack down on predatory businesses that exploit our vets
— Invest in mental healthcare and suicide prevention
I'm committed to making New Mexico the best state in the country to be stationed and retire after service so military families can build their future here with stability, opportunity, and support. This Memorial Day, let us honor those who made the ultimate sacrifice not only with our gratitude, but with our commitment to stand by the veterans, service members, and military families who continue to serve our country every day.
I will never stop fighting for the people who fight for us. Thank you,
Deb

| | | | | | Friend,
Memorial Day is a time to pause and remember the brave men and women of our armed forces who gave their lives to defend our freedom. It’s thanks to their service and sacrifice that we live in the greatest nation in the world.
This morning, I was honored to attend the Manchester VA’s Memorial Day Ceremony with many of our veterans and their families, and later today, I’ll be joining leaders in Manchester to dedicate a new memorial to those killed in the Gulf War and the War on Terror. While we owe our fallen service members a debt that can never be repaid, I’m proud of the way New Hampshire honors these men and women.
As you gather with friends and family today, I hope you’ll take a moment to remember those we’ve lost and the families who miss them every day. Freedom isn’t free, and today is about those who made the ultimate sacrifice in defense of the freedoms we enjoy every day.
Thank you for joining me today in remembering these brave service members.
All the best,
Kelly

| Friends and Supporters,
_When I’m elected as your state senator, I will raise my right hand and take an oath to uphold and protect the United States Constitution_. **Today we honor the memory and sacrifice of men and women who took that same oath, and defended it with their lives.** _Memorial Day ought to give every American pause_ , to stop and consider whether we have done enough to measure up to the standard that’s been set. The _liberty and prosperity_ that you and I are able to enjoy every day living in LD27 was paid for by generations of _soldiers_ , _sailors_ , _airmen_ , _Marines_ , and _National Guardsmen_ who answered the call of service when their country called.
---
|

subject: Direct from the White House:
body:
A humbling message...
| Patriot,
---
I’m truly humbled and honored.
---
Direct from the White House, my friend President Trump said:
---
**“JIM JORDAN IS A VERY GOOD FRIEND, FIGHTER, AND WINNER... HE WILL _NEVER_ LET YOU DOWN”**
---
[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=61735e119eda4de19bbf7c4af22ea9a8&_e=n4jrOMuaHfkZ2hoxcfsfsZl6ui-MoxzXcS7aZt882ivxLUdjZa_dAl974nSeBz5y3YJNEaVL9AzY5-k6coY-T9aFaIU9n2z9QJNmR982REVcZH1C0s-alrr2YlrnSu-hxvCVm5T50krFEXVgzqtNvum3S73bWiIKMNWfrKAy4O6N3JlvSJnUgTPv_sC9NKfgJhTYFE33KcXHP6SrY2EBGtf-DZB_GiADaPZ5PcAIlFahV87Z3q3pOo73qbtCjCjrQH_TZDZ0n5jSu1PmZUR7vpDlGriVukvuW_bC5ZsMtr8206p67a9vV53R_UPHhUKMkFRRh5fFyjaoh1E2X2yiUU2q7v5xHpj29KN2pKsIDdIFIljwIsv7hIEo0pxWjRqa2XD8_13WGRFfFdmGMXS-Xp8QCH0avhpLEDW1k5nvqBj3UZAfvlA98FghhyD80id4kr5NfrNmXXU6wN5wLcTRQ9-54flk-GcMwIVb8EB2RCzee7oqUyG7dOfQc7ScA7mWB5lmm8TTe2yjA4laM8xKqm0vmdDNxzvg8a8GTNMR2lHudN-jaxN-njGLFnT4L-R3O7p78SfE6zdEUbAKHvwalw%3D%3D)
---
Coming from the President, those are powerful words.
---
President Trump knows _better than anyone_ the fight I’m waging to drain the swamp and put power back where it belongs – with _YOU_ , the American people.
---
Look, I know talk is cheap in politics. Anyone can make a promise. Anyone can say they’ll fight.
---
**But I’ve got the receipts to back it up**. I’ve been sued. I’ve been spied on. My phone records were seized. And the Left only attacks me, because I fight for YOU.
---
**I’m working with the President – _behind the scenes and all hours of the day_ – to deliver on the agenda you voted for.**
---
And directly from the Oval Office, President Trump laid out the agenda **WE** are fighting for:
---
_**✅Grow our economy
✅Cut taxes
✅Slash burdensome regulations
✅Promote Made-In-The-USA products
✅Champion American energy dominance
✅Keep our border secure
✅Stop migrant crime
✅Defend your constitutional rights
✅Stopping the Radical Left ** _
---
And in just a few months, that same agenda will be voted on AGAIN in the midterm elections.
---
There’s been a lot of doom and gloom about our odds of holding the House. But truth be told, Democrats now ONLY have a **2-POINT** advantage over us.
---
And that’s not because voters suddenly approve of Radical Left ideas._It’s simply because our side isn’t showing up to vote._
---
**If 2% more Republicans show up, we can EASILY erase the Democrats’ 2-point lead. This is a problem we can absolutely fix.**
---
_So, we are going zip code by zip code in our voter file to determine where we need more participation._
---
Patriot, we’ve crunched the numbers and with our razor-thin majority now within the margin of error, YOUR voter profile in your zip code is the difference maker.
---
_That’s why I’m reaching out today to simply ask that you VERIFY your GOP voter profile to give me and President Trump the most accurate polling possible to ERASE the Democrats’ 2% LEAD over us._
---

**FIRST:** **Something is shifting in Texas.** Since January, we’ve seen races flip that Democrats usually don’t win here. Deep-red local and state seats are flipping because Texans are tired of being left behind by poor Republican leadership, and they want change.
**THEN:** **Millions of grassroots supporters have stepped up to build the team that can beat Greg Abbott in November** and deliver the affordable future working families deserve. And the numbers are reflecting that momentum. Recent polling has Gina within just 3 points of Abbott, one of the closest margins we’ve seen.
**NOW: Abbott and Republicans are taking notice of the shift happening in Texas — and they’re intimidated.** Abbott has already said he’s planning to spend _**$25 million in Harris County alone** _to try to drag it back into the red column. And we should expect the same strategy to happen across Texas.
That is exactly why we set a goal of raising **$100,000** before Sunday. We have to prove we can compete everywhere, respond fast, and keep building the campaign Texans are ready for.

This Memorial Day, I'm thinking about the Arizonans who gave everything in service to this country.

I'm thinking about the families in Yuma, Tucson, Sierra Vista, and communities across our state who have sent sons and daughters, mothers and fathers, brothers and sisters into harm's way — trusting that the democracy they were defending would still be standing when they came home.

I'm thinking about what it means to honor that sacrifice, not just with words, but with action.

The men and women who have served this country didn't fight for a democracy reserved for the few. They fought for free and fair elections. For the right of every American, regardless of race, zip code, or income, to have an equal voice. For a government that is accountable to its people, not the other way around

That is the democracy we are fighting to protect today.

Arizona has always been a state of service. We have one of the highest concentrations of veterans and military families in the nation. We know what sacrifice looks like — and we know what it demands of those of us still in the fight.

So today, we pause to honor the fallen, and we recommit to the work of making sure that what they gave their lives for — democracy, freedom, and dignity for all — is never taken for granted.

Thank you for being a part of that work.

With gratitude,

Charlene Fernandez

Memorial Day is a time to honor and mourn the U.S. military personnel who lost their lives in service to our country, including the women who have served throughout American history — often long before they were formally acknowledged or accepted.
After the Civil War, Memorial Day became an official day of remembrance for the Americans who died in service, including the estimated 400 to 1,000 women who secretly fought by disguising themselves as men. One of the most notable was Sarah Emma Edmonds, who enlisted in the 2nd Michigan Infantry under the name Franklin Flint Thompson, and later became the only woman to receive a veteran’s pension for Civil War service. Reflecting on her decision to serve, she wrote, “I could only thank God that I was free and could go forward and work, and I was not obliged to stay at home and weep.”
Her story represents only a fraction of the over 3 million women who have served in or alongside the armed forces since the American Revolution.
At Emerge, we believe representation matters because stories like these matter. By recognizing the women who have served, sacrificed, and paved the way for future generations, we continue the work of ensuring their contributions are seen, remembered, and celebrated.
-Emerge HQ

subject: Honoring the brave

body:
# [#]
Peter,

On this Memorial Day, let’s honor the brave men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country and ensure their legacy is never forgotten.

This Memorial Day, I’m recommitting to upholding the values and freedoms they fought and died for and ensuring that our men and women who are able to return home from the battlefield are taken care of by the country they served. That means fighting for their healthcare, adequate housing, and mental health services.

As a combat veteran myself, I’ll never stop working to serve our fallen heroes, veterans and their families. We owe them endless gratitude.

Please join me in honoring those who gave their lives for our country.

Thank you,

Mike Thompson

body:
On Memorial Day, we honor the Americans who made the ultimate sacrifice.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019e6028dc1e-a055f317-bbb3-49db-8a94-7f7aca67a043-000000/VWqYDcPecA8cX2VnyH83XZocQ7D0yFeM5hS9Pp8_BLQ=452)Patriot–Today, we remember the men and women of the U.S. military who gave their lives in service to our country.We remember those who left behind parents, spouses, children, friends, and entire lives that should have continued. Americans who answered the call to serve and sacrificed everything for the rest of us.For many families, Memorial Day is not abstract or symbolic. It is personal. There are people across this country who still carry the loss of someone they loved.Memorial Day is about honoring the American heroes who died for our freedom, including the freedom to gather with family and enjoy an afternoon together. Our ability to live ordinary American lives in peace exists because others were willing to sacrifice everything for it.Freedom has always come at a cost, and there are families across this country who know that cost firsthand. Some of you reading this email have lived through that loss yourselves.No words can fully repay a sacrifice like that. The best we can do is remember them faithfully, honor the lives they lived, and fight to remain a nation worthy of the lives they gave.To every Gold Star family, and to every person carrying the loss of someone who served and never returned home, please know that today we remember them with sincere gratitude and respect.May God bless the memory of the fallen, comfort the families who mourn them, and continue to bless the United States of America.In grateful remembrance,Jenny Beth Martin _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. # YOUR “HEALTHY” BREAKFAST IS BACKFIRING
---
| | | | |
---
Most Americans believe fruit is always healthy.

But what if the way you’re eating it is doing the **exact opposite**?

According to Dr. Steven Gundry, a [single breakfast mistake](https://links.mail.newgrowthzones.com/u/click?_t=95eaeb593eae452fa9211d49d8360695&_m=b14474472cbd41d69fc2ccbb51e51b9e&_e=VUiMHCr_iA9UA-D4eiqtWd0bP7jdcRyZsA0dV0BnqaTcB4ofz4HgioD4wM1tRNsrw7nCsQkyB_VZni1w_8iVfzw9h4aW7T724ezkRzUidxKcLZjH4V_7M2p4623LMUe9wdSD0ycLRGvvHHS-hvT8lxqrgOiOfKEsafaf0YuAmq6Jv7Fp2BwyP3sjoTcm4xioj7SucDwNyFhk9leYsYEPiFZI6R84Y_VgFQqKMHiAHaVmnzvIU_wd6vOHOouBpDJMkYvKvX_Tzm-18hprkUU4OtK2C1iQNeIA-l4RDEEFF6OpNDOppS42HwbOqFsE5xZRwTRqlnLN2kKktgLwi09To3Afx7qtFALOfCD07UMsB7jjPNP1_3qMw4lSB5o4gAK2iqZTsQtTga1HOnoWRx8xGeTgKG4yJ84L7ED92e7PyN1nF9Xc-8lYx9oYlolK475tUzRSq1ToPF4-55hFlIbZG_aI7KqFBNZPK8RFU93z1rl5VHll368vYGoPN6e_IoCC0qgfdzI4Bcg3Nx7T7JIlCqzqClTfAuH61ZdCT27Oto4oiVylccP-QAuQOuOYwRs1Gz6-2fNOjW_h7MQyL3TrJQ%3D%3D) is causing millions of people to unknowingly turn fruit into something that **spikes fatigue, fogs the brain, and wrecks digestion**.

# Jamie Dimon warns Mamdani: Grow, or jobs flee
JPMorgan Chase leader Jamie Dimon cautioned New York City's mayor Zohran Mamdani that success depends on **[creating conditions for businesses and families to thrive](https://substack.com/redirect/2e329c1c-157e-4f51-b2bc-315f7b8ae091?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rather than relying on ideological messaging or risk continued departures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e329c1c-157e-4f51-b2bc-315f7b8ae091?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Competition Applies Everywhere:** Dimon stated that leaders must treat their location as one among many rivals in culture, research, education, and livability so residents and companies choose to remain and expand.
**Results Matter Most:** After the recent discussion the executive made clear his judgment will rest solely on measurable improvements instead of any talk centered on fairness or principles.
**Texas Now Leads Employment:** The bank maintains a larger workforce inside Texas than within New York City itself, demonstrating how decisions follow practical advantages.
**Discussion Covered Efficiency:** The conversation at headquarters addressed cutting unnecessary spending, simplifying approval processes, and increasing joint efforts between government and private groups.

# Gold Rises 1% on U.S.-Iran Deal hopes
Bullion **[gained more than one percent Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/cf3a5a84-ae6f-47f8-b9ca-46e60c15585c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** because expectations of possible progress toward a U.S.-Iran agreement reduced pressure on both the dollar and crude values, thereby softening inflation forecasts.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cf3a5a84-ae6f-47f8-b9ca-46e60c15585c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Spot Price Moves Higher:** Gold in the spot market increased one-point-one percent to four-thousand-five-hundred-fifty-nine dollars and seven cents per ounce while futures for June delivery rose zero-point-eight percent to four-thousand-five-hundred-fifty-nine dollars and eighty cents.
**Deal Prospects Weigh on Oil:** Investor optimism around an eventual reopening of the critical sea passage has helped pull crude lower and eased associated cost concerns.
**Greenback Softens:** Currency trading placed the dollar near its weakest level in a full week, making the metal more accessible for international buyers.
**Broader Metals Follow:** Silver posted a three-point-one percent increase to seventy-seven dollars and seventy-nine cents, platinum advanced two-point-three percent, and palladium rose two-point-seven percent.

# Lockheed unveils AI Tech to stop drone swarms
Lockheed Martin chief Jim Taiclet described newly developed artificial-intelligence capabilities **[engineered to locate, evaluate, and neutralize groups of hostile drones](https://substack.com/redirect/873d7461-a4b3-488f-b414-de3d8c8b95d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the company pushes forward on modern defense systems.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/873d7461-a4b3-488f-b414-de3d8c8b95d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Sanctum Handles Detection:** The platform employs artificial intelligence to identify incoming threats, assess risk, and forecast movement before any engagement occurs.
**MORFIUS Targets Multiple Units:** This mobile system approaches small hostile aircraft and disables them through directed energy pulses, enabling one flight to address as many as fifty targets without traditional munitions.
**Nvidia Provides Core Hardware:** A collaboration supplies the specialized processors required for these security-focused artificial-intelligence operations that the firm first centralized internally during 2020.
**Missiles Receive New Role:** Older air-to-ground munitions were modified into ground-launched interceptors offering lower expense and greater scalability when linked to the artificial-intelligence platform.
* * *
* * *
# Oil at "tank bottoms" in Asia warns veteran strategist
Veteran strategist Jeff Currie reported that available oil supplies in Asia **[have reached critically low operating thresholds,](https://substack.com/redirect/8494d72a-3bff-4125-a0e2-696a166cda86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** warning Europe faces the same risk shortly and the United States could see issues emerge by July because of the ongoing conflict.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8494d72a-3bff-4125-a0e2-696a166cda86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Stockpile Numbers Mislead:** Global inventory reports often overlook that much of the material must stay committed to keep pipelines and facilities functioning properly and cannot enter immediate market use.
**Regional Product Prices Spike:** In Singapore area costs for diesel have overtaken jet fuel after earlier shifts, showing the pressure continues to evolve across fuels.
**Europe Timeline Short:** Currie projects the next wave of strain will hit Europe in roughly one month while July becomes the point of concern domestically once summer driving demand intensifies.
**Hormuz Key to Relief:** The strategist stressed that restoring flow through the vital waterway offers the sole lasting answer, though current drawdowns continue to improve Iran's bargaining strength daily.

# Mandalorian and Grogu is the lowest Disney Star Wars opening
The latest big-screen entry from the popular series brought in roughly eighty-two million dollars domestically across its opening three days, marking the **[smallest initial theatrical result for any Star Wars project](https://substack.com/redirect/bf20bc37-8e03-455b-8885-80c76fce077a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/bf20bc37-8e03-455b-8885-80c76fce077a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)released by the studio.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bf20bc37-8e03-455b-8885-80c76fce077a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. | | | | | |
An insider poll just landed on our desk. It covered the biggest races in New Mexico. The results aren't what people expect.
[We had the pollster on to break it all down — and tell us who actually wins.](https://us.list-manage.com/jP0yCpAp0tX?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/weO4CFNBR8R?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🔥 **INSIDER POLL: GREGG HULL 33, DOUG TURNER 30, DUKE RODRIGUEZ 12 — 25% UNDECIDED**
Nicole McCleskey of Public Opinion Strategies — the pollster behind Susana Martinez and 13 gubernatorial races in 2022 — joined us with her husband Jay, one of New Mexico's top GOP strategists, to break down the numbers on Gregg Hull, Doug Turner, and Duke Rodriguez.
The horse race number tells one story. The favorability numbers tell a completely different one. And there's a specific stat about Duke that tells you why he can't win this race no matter what he does from here.
Then she made her call. Jay did too. One person at our table didn't agree — and you'll never guess who.

🚨 **HULL'S CAMPAIGN HAS A PROBLEM. SO DOES TURNER.**
Turner is attacking. Hull is not responding. That math doesn't end well in any campaign we've ever seen.
The regional breakdown is even more revealing. There's one part of New Mexico where Turner is up 30 points on Hull. There's another part where Hull is up 27. We show you the map.
If Hull doesn't change something fast, the pollster says this could be a 20-point race. The wrong direction.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/wS0l2ZxQdUs?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
📉 **TRUMP'S APPROVAL JUST HIT A NUMBER NO PRESIDENT HAS SEEN IN 17 YEARS**
37%. The NYT/Siena poll just dropped, and it's the lowest second-term number in nearly two decades. Underwater on immigration — his strongest issue a year ago. Underwater on cost of living. Underwater everywhere.
What that means for whoever wins the Republican primary in New Mexico is the conversation every campaign in the country is having right now. We had it on the show.

⛽ **DEB HAALAND TRIED TO ANSWER A FRACKING QUESTION. IT DIDN'T GO WELL.**
KRQE's Jessica Garate asked a yes-or-no question. The former Interior Secretary couldn't get there. Then Jessica asked a follow-up.
When you see what banning fracking on public lands actually means for New Mexico schools, you'll understand why she didn't want to answer the first time.
---

| |

That is the President of the United States, on the record, saying: pass the SAVE America Act NOW. Use the Housing Bill. Use the FISA Bill. Get it done.

And he is right.

**Maryland just had 500,000 fake mail-in ballots exposed.** Not five hundred. Not five thousand. FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND. That is a whole city's worth of crooked ballots in one blue state.

The President is demanding action. The American people are demanding action. And what are Senate Democrats doing?

They are hiding behind the zombie filibuster.

That is what I call it. The filibuster used to mean something. A senator had to stand on the Senate floor, hold the microphone, and make his case out loud. Today? Schumer's team can just send a one-line email and kill any bill they don't like — without ever showing their face on camera.

It is cowardly. It is dishonest. And it is killing this country.

That is why the President is right to demand we put the SAVE America Act inside the Housing and FISA bills. Those bills have to pass. If Democrats want to shut down housing and surveillance authority over election integrity, let them try to explain that to the American people in broad daylight.

| | | | | Peter,

I wanted to thank you for your support from the very beginning, personally.

**Without you, I would not be ANYWHERE close to where I am today.**

You stood with President Trump during his first term and you've been with him every step of the way during his second term.

You stood with me when I was enacting President Trump's America First agenda every day over the past couple of years.

And since I announced my candidacy for Governor of Florida, you've been with me through it all.

The attacks, the lies, and the smears by the Radical Left and its allies in the Fake News media.

**Together, we have shown what it really means to love our country and be PROUD Americans.**

And I wanted to let you know that your support hasn't gone unnoticed.

BUT, your support is needed more than ever.

My Primary is **ALMOST HERE** , and I need you by my side to keep the momentum going for MAGA come November.

Democrats are fighting tooth and nail to HALT our momentum and SILENCE Republican voices like ours.

The stakes are growing, and every cent matters.

That's why I'm asking**ONE FINAL TIME** for you to chip in anything you can afford today and stand with me in my fight to **KEEP MAGA STRONG!**

name: Seth Moulton
subject: What Memorial Day means to a veteran.
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/74758/images/Email%20Wrapper%20Header%203.png]

Friend,

Memorial Day has always meant something different to me than it does to most people. I think about the Marines I served with: the ones who didn't come home, and the ones who did, but came back different.

I think about what the war actually cost, not in dollars and not in policy terms, but in human lives and human families. I joined the Marines days after graduating from college, months before 9/11. I didn't know what was coming. None of us did. But I knew I wanted to serve, so that nobody else would have to go in my place.

Four combat tours in Iraq later, I came home with a deepened belief that service matters, that leadership matters, and that the people who send others into harm's way have a grave obligation to get it right.

Those years also gave me something I didn't expect: some of the closest friendships of my life. The Marines I led came from every corner of America, all from different backgrounds. Through shared hardship, they became family. War is a place of profound contradictions. The worst days of my life happened overseas. So did some of the best, because of the people I was surrounded by.

The hardest question my Marines ever asked me was: "Sir, why are we risking our lives for this?" My answer then, and the one that carried us through, was simple: we're here so that nobody has to go in our place.

That's what I keep coming back to. We honor the fallen by being there for each other, by caring for the veterans who made it home but carry invisible wounds, by rejecting the division that threatens to tear us apart, and by proving that the nation they gave everything for is worthy of their sacrifice.

Today I'll be thinking about the people who gave everything. I hope you'll take a moment to do the same.

- Seth
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/74758/images/moulton-header-headshot-3.jpg]

Seth Moulton is a Marine and a Democrat with a mission to bring a new generation of leaders to Congress. Seth’s two young daughters, Emmy and Caroline, remind him every day why new leadership and urgent action can’t wait any longer.

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: Honoring Their Sacrifice
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
Memorial Day is a time to honor the brave men and women who gave their lives in service to our country.....

| | | | | |
---
| |

Dear Peter,Today, we pause.Not for celebration, but for remembrance.Memorial Day is a time to honor the brave men and women who gave their lives in service to our country. It is because of their sacrifice that we enjoy the freedoms we often take for granted.Behind every flag placed at a grave, there is a story.
A life of courage.
A family forever changed.This day is not about politics. It is not about division. There is no ask, because today is about gratitude.It is about remembering those who stepped forward, knowing the cost, and served anyway.As we gather with family and friends today, I hope we each take a moment to reflect on what this day truly represents. Freedom is not free. It has been earned through the sacrifice of generations of Americans who believed in something greater than themselves.To the families who carry that loss every day, we honor you.
To those who served alongside them, we remember.And to those who gave everything, we will never forget.
With gratitude,
**Karen Crnkovich** Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: This is about filling the fossil fuel industry’s pockets
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
The Trump administration is lying to you about the impact of climate change.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260525-6275-footer&t=1&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)
The climate crisis is here, Peter.
It’s a reality millions are living through right now. Wildfires swallowing up entire towns, floods leaving communities devastated, and unbearable heatwaves pouring into your home.
**And instead of acting with the urgency this moment demands, Trump’s DOE just commissioned a fake report designed to cover up the real and pressing impacts of climate change.**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260525.Nh5Um5&refcode=em20260525-6275&t=2&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)
I want to be clear — this is about filling the fossil fuel industry’s pockets.
The EPA used this fake report to dismantle the legal foundation holding polluters accountable. Undermining and eliminating regulations so the fossil fuel industry can continue to poison our air and water without consequences.
Trump’s DOE just stripped our protections away, and working families will pay the price. Because when the DOE deliberately distorts climate data, it becomes that much harder to fund disaster relief, invest in clean energy, and provide environmental protections our communities depend on to survive.
[**If that makes you as angry as I am, pitch in $3 now to help me keep fighting back against these climate deniers in Congress.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260525.Nh5Um5&refcode=em20260525-6275&amount=3&t=3&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)
**What’s even more infuriating? The DOE’s own internal scientists reviewed this report and rejected it.**
_They called it misleading. Unjustified. Hypocritical._
More than 85 independent climate scientists issued a formal rebuttal to it. But this administration doesn’t care. They got what they needed: a stamp of approval for the fossil fuel industry to keep on polluting, no matter who’s left to suffer the consequences.
I refuse to let this administration bury the truth. I refuse to let them prioritize corporate profits over the safety of everyday people — and over the future of this planet.
[**If you’re able, will you pitch in $3 to help keep me in Congress fighting for our communities and our planet?** ](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260525.Nh5Um5&refcode=em20260525-6275&amount=3&t=4&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260525.Nh5Um5&amount=3&refcode=em20260525-6275&t=23&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)**
With gratitude,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260525-6275-footer&t=24&refcode2=6275_420207_9qYVUc&akid=6275%2E420207%2E9qYVUc)**

Happy Memorial Day,
Today we honor the fallen – the brave Americans who stood up for something bigger than themselves and who gave their lives to protect the values and freedoms we hold dear.
Their legacy isn't just in history books. It lives in the communities they served, the families they loved, and the democracy they died to defend.
The best way we can honor them is to protect what they fought for — to show up, to speak out, and to keep working toward the America they believed in so much that they were willing to make the ultimate sacrifice.
That's exactly what this campaign is about.
Thank you for being a part of this effort. And thank you to every veteran and military family in our community – your service and your sacrifice will never be forgotten.
With Gratitude,

body:
Two young sisters were rescued from trafficking. Your gift helps protect vulnerable children from unimaginable evil.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e936921/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvNURjajlWald5RA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA1MjU/LbmNsNXFQU1p6YQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNvb01TTDk2aXJNdjVscw/gahShTA/sagbe9f7b72)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
| | | Friend,
---
My heart is heavy as I write this. Two little sisters in Uganda, ages 13 and 9, were found shaking in silence behind a locked door. Their eyes were hollow. Their voices had gone quiet long before rescuers arrived. It started with something that could happen in almost any family. An argument at home.
The girls ran away scared and alone. Then a man appeared and offered to help. For a moment, it probably felt like an answer to prayer. **Instead, it was a trap.**
**He locked them in a room for days.**
**No way out - just fear and the crushing thought that no one was coming.** **But someone _did_ come.** A local worker heard suspicious noises and called the police.**** Then a **Sound of Freedom Foundation** rescue partner was contacted to help.
---
If you’ve never heard of us before, the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is a faith-driven movement. We're dedicated to **stopping the sale of God’s children** and helping protect vulnerable children from trafficking and exploitation.
---
[ Give Now to Protect God’s Children ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
My name is Eduardo Verástegui. After years of working alongside rescuers and hearing firsthand what trafficked children endure, our mission grew out of the _Sound of Freedom_ film I produced. Because supporters stepped forward, trained responders were ready when these girls needed help most. Police broke down the door and the suspect was arrested. And while officers secured the scene, a social worker knelt beside those frightened girls and whispered: **“You are safe now.”**
**“You are not alone.”**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**Friend, this is what your support makes possible.**

**Not just rescue, but healing, protection and care.**
---
After children are rescued, the trauma does not disappear overnight. The two sisters needed medical care, counseling, safe shelter and advocates to help them through police interviews and court proceedings. **They needed a place where they could simply be children again.** **And thanks to compassionate people who refused to look away, they received it.**
---
At the **Sound of Freedom Foundation,** we work to help stop trafficking through five areas of action:
---
* **Prevention** to strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children

* **Intervention** that equips trusted rescue partners to save exploited children

There was a time in America when common sense did not need a press conference, a political campaign, or a courtroom defense. It was simply understood. Men were men. Women were women. Parents were responsible for their children. Criminals were supposed to be punished. Work was better than welfare. Truth mattered. The flag was respected. Faith was honored. Freedom came with responsibility. And government existed to protect liberty, not replace personal duty. But somewhere along the way, America began to drift from the simple truths that built this nation. We have watched a war develop against common sense itself. It is not just a political disagreement. It is a cultural battle over reality, morality, responsibility, and truth. The Founding Fathers understood something that many modern leaders seem to have forgotten: a free country cannot survive if its people lose their moral foundation.

| | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSrn4JnyYtk1EREaCYHldIw2Es-lCsKe-k7RYeRErCjUmpL6YWg0aqprxBCSlqaUKjL6uf8EDq6vQVEaFZEFWaTvOKtPnFc2PEalY2SnM4_7Vl5lVxHfZCJu6tLF7DXMSIontUMgjKXBXm4CHKPJarTnpwYNzHIxfmlYfnyWpDPfX_bxQ-quQtobX4EtSFcG3X8tBhzO6cg9Vd3jTakzJAIlSPzstsKroGnaKZU3f0QHA/4qx/rmLnrt2lQ3WJ3pnmYhwciQ/h0/h001.zpLBdbeFHdMfUAQDkeM1aAi0Ehy5anDGDrqWrcqZomo)
